INCOMPLETE -- structural no-win, deliberately. Journey to Alpha Centauri (In Real Time), Julian Fleetwood 1998, subtitled "An Interactive Waste of Time". This is a best-effort CHECKPOINT, not a win: it is deterministic (identical transcript for seeds 1/2/99/12345 and unseeded), stops with no trailing command, and ends on SCORE so the corpus records the game's own 0/100 scoreboard. Proof that no win is reachable: the story file has exactly ONE writer of the Inform deadflag -- txd 9e04 (property 44 = each_turn on the Control Room, obj 24) does "if G86==1 { G0D=100; G13=2; print S108 }", where S108 is "Welcome to Alpha Centauri. Now go home."; no routine ever stores deadflag 1 or 3, so the game has no death and no other ending. G86 is written only by the countdown routine 9e2c, which sets it to 1 only when the five counter globals G88..G8C are all zero; 9e2c otherwise decrements the mixed-radix counter by exactly one (60s / 60m / 24h / 365d / 3000y, initial values at 0x089b..0x08a3). 9e2c is called only from the status-line routine 9fe0, which the library invokes from the real-time timed read (txd 4642: "read local0 local1 #0a 9f3c" -- 10 tenths = one tick per real second, the game's whole gimmick) and from the YesOrNo/keypress prompts at 6e43/7536/864f. From the initial globals the counter needs 102,175,497,149 calls to reach all-zero plus one more to set G86 = 102,175,497,150 ticks, i.e. about 3,238 years of real time (closed form validated against a literal simulation of 9e2c). Under Jericho the timed interrupt never fires at all, so the only tick source is a YesOrNo prompt (about one tick per two commands, ~2.0e11 commands). RAM instrumentation confirms it: no ordinary turn moves the counter, and an exhaustive single-action sweep of all 177 grammar verb words x 7 noun forms (1,239 commands) moved neither score, deadflag, arrival flag nor counter and never produced done/victory/game_over. A diagnostic RAM patch (zeroing G88..G8C, NOT part of this route) confirms the terminal itself is intact and fires "Welcome to Alpha Centauri. Now go home. *** You have won *** In that game you scored 100 out of a possible 100" -- so this is a real custom-flavoured library win that is simply unreachable, not a missing ending. The author says so himself in the shipped HELP menu, which this route displays in full: subject 4 quotes Terry Pratchett's Only You Can Save Mankind ("if anyone kept their computer on for three thousand years, they'd be rewarded by ... a message saying, 'Welcome to Alpha Centauri. Conan Kill Everything (Ian Haberkorn, 2005; Inform v6.30/Library 6/11, Release 2, serial 050428). A one-room comedic 'massacre' game whose entire object of play is to KILL EVERYTHING in the dungeon set. Authored victory ending 'It's a wrap!' (string s125: 'This was true drama, world class! ... you have a great career coming your way...') at score 15/15 in 25 turns. Because the win is implemented via the death deadflag (self-kill routine r0295 sets deadflag global g18=#03 after incrementing score to 15), Jericho reports done=False/victory=False and get_max_score()=0; the true score is 15/15, confirmed by the end banner 'Conan scored 15 out of a possible 15'. The intended solution is embedded verbatim in the game as an AMUSING string (s266): 'kill cat / kill golem / kill spider / kill wizard / x hat, turn dial, tap hat / eat apple / look, wait (until fly lands), kill fly, wait, wait, wait, kill spider / remove cloth, kill cloth / x table, x hole, kill worm with pin / kill pin / kill door / climb table, kill torch / kill table / kill sword / kill self / Conan killed everything!'. Mechanics: bare 'kill X' uses Conan's sword. The wizard summons wildcat->golem->little spider; chopping the little spider makes it flee into a ceiling crack, which then lets you slay the wizard. 'turn dial' then 'tap hat' disarms the magic hat (tapping it un-turned teleports Conan to his death, s249). 'eat apple' kills the apple. The fly can only be squashed on a turn when it has just landed (s188 vs s187); its dead body lures the little spider down from the crack (s199-s202) so it becomes reachable and killable (s205). Removing the loincloth yields the bone pin used to stab the woodworm in the table's hole; the pin is then snapped. Room fixtures (torch/table/sword/self) are gated: Conan 'does not want to do this - now' until every creature is dead, and the torch requires 'climb table' first (killing it plunges the room into darkness). Killing the sword leaves broken fragments that Conan uses for the final self-kill. Deterministic under seed=1 (fly-landing RNG): two fresh replays produced byte-identical run.py transcripts, SHA256 f41fdbf5a92c77b1a8579df46fce308ad015ea4483c54fab1886ccdf289fcec8. You are now elected to the cottage council.' fires the moment the last treasure is swallowed by the beach-house machine; 'Thorvald says: - Welcome back!' and 'Press Enter to quit the game:' follow. Scoring model (decoded from the story file): base 50, plus nine scoring tasks -- entering the hall +5, cutting open the Foam-rubber room window with the diamond +10, cutting the curtain with the scissors +20, kicking the inflated ball through the ceiling window of the room with holes everywhere +10, obtaining the phone directory +5, taking part in the Muppet Show debate +30, making the guard unlock the ornate gate +10, digging up the pirate's cache +10, putting the corpse in the grave +25 -- plus 160 points for the eleven treasures dropped in the beach house (diamond 15, cucumber 5, silver ingot 10, gold coins 10, trilogy 10, contract 15, laurel wreath 15, pearl necklace 25, halberd 20, alarm clock 15, skull 20). The faun shoe is a deliberate red herring: it must be staked in the gambling machine for the gold coins instead of being dropped. Route outline: enter the front door (+5), take the ball and the laurel wreath; row the boat from the east shore to the southern shore so the beach house becomes reachable by land for the rest of the game (the alternative entrance from the right chamber is a 60% instant death); fall through the bathing hut into Thorvald's room, take the diamond, CUT WINDOW / DIAMOND in the Foam-rubber room for the crowbar (+10), prize the chest open for the cycle pump, inflate the ball, fetch the ladder from the dark wardrobe and OPEN HATCH for the cucumber, hand the wreath to the old man and take his water bottle, OPEN WARDROBE + CORKSCREW for the silver ingot; take the spade in the cemetery, the faun shoe in the Swiss clock room, PULL LEVER for the gold coins, fill the water bottle; bank four treasures in the beach house; take the keys, UNLOCK CASE for the sledgehammer, BREAK BOX for the scissors, CUT CURTAIN (+20); KICK BALL at the ceiling window (+10) and climb the rope to the dark passage for the vodka bottle; take the trilogy, then TAKE / STAY in the pitch-dark passage to keep the lamp; GIVE WATER, BLIND OLD MAN, TAKE PEARL NECKLACE, ALEA JACTA EST to send the wreath back to the studio; the Muppet Show (name / PERFORM / SING / FOLLOW / interest / RIGHT / DISCUSS) yields Kermit's contract and the debate (+30); UNPLUG / PLUG IN / UNPLUG / PLUG IN the telephone for the directory (+5); GIVE VODKA to the guard, TAKE HALBERD, GIVE KEYS, TAKE GUARD, then UNLOCK GATE (+10) and loot the alarm clock from the Council's dining room; walk the still-drunk guard to the ZZZZ room where Fozzi refills the vodka bottle, GIVE VODKA again so he falls asleep, KILL GUARD, carry the corpse to the grave and drop it (+25); DIG the pirate's cache (+10) and recover the four treasures he stole; bank six treasures; return to the grave after the 30-turn decay to collect the skull and drop it for the final 20 points. Determinism: seed=1 is pinned and required -- the game is full of RNG (a roaming pirate who steals carried treasures once the turn counter passes 50, a 70%-per-visit vodka refill, a 4/7 Muppet branch, the old man teleporting to a random room, a rotating labyrinth), and several steps in this route are RNG-aligned by deliberate filler turns (four LOOKs in the vestibule align the vodka refill and its exit door). Five full-through-quit replays were byte-identical before the trailing quit input was removed (sha256 bb418b812fcc6382c9a82c36fe9f282e8644052d98de5320aef3102b1fec6759); the normalized corpus audit also wins and ends on DROP SKULL (transcript sha256 4d8a3d92904f8893886d610a1ba404ed8a387963706afd88c305ac8525c4894d). The three '\\t' entries are dumb-frotz's documented runtime escape 'advance clock just enough to time out the current input'. Cottage genuinely uses Z-machine timed input for its 'Be quiet, I'm sleeping/waiting/digging' pauses (routine r0059 issues a read with a one-second interrupt routine), which a human clears by simply not typing; Jericho always supplies a line immediately, so without this escape the pause can never expire and the game is unfinishable. They appear only while such a pause is pending: after the crowbar knocks you out, while waiting for the lamp, and while digging. Parser notes: outdoors uses compass directions and indoors uses FORWARD/BACK/LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN; 'southeast' is matched as SOUTH by the hand-written parser, so the two-letter diagonals must be used. The front door has to be OPENed each time. Prelude entries are page responses: two Enters accept the default date [15-JUL-2009] and time [19:00] and 'yes' answers 'Have you ventured inside before?'.

Solution: ERASE PENTAGRAM FROM FLOOR (the 'erase pentag from NOUN' grammar; frees the egg), TAKE AXE, HIT EGG WITH AXE to shatter it down to the raw yolk ('contents of the egg'), then cook it: BURN YOLK WITH RING -- the gold ring is a fire giant's ring and its magical heat fries the yolk (sets the 'cooked' attribute; R0174 action #37 -> 'The egg sizzles'). EAT YOLK now succeeds ('The fried egg is delicious', +146 -> 500) because the cooked guard passes (R0174 action #23). A couple of turns later digestion completes (R0176 sets the win flag G06=#1e) and the endgame banner prints S101 ('...impervious to injury. You can now begin your quest to rule the world!') -> max score 500/500. Two WAITs let the digestion daemon fire. Note: the ring activates with the special 'ring, on' command and becomes too hot to hold, but burning the yolk with the (un-activated) magic ring is what the puzzle wants. Win logic reverse-engineered from txd (R0174 cook+eat, R0176 digest-win, R0185 end banner). notes: Solved entirely via live Jericho 3.3.1 replay plus static disassembly (txd/infodump) of Erden.z8 -- no external walkthroughs consulted, only in-game/shipped hints. The game is confirmed scoreless (score always 0/0 throughout); its win condition is a custom text ending, not a score threshold or deadflag=2 auto-win, so Jericho's victory()/env.step() 'done' flag never flips True here (confirmed both live and by design: exploration_strategy.md notes such unbound large-game-collection titles need banner text recognised manually). Winning sequence (this route's final chain, extending the previously-preserved 64-command partial that ended at 'take dragon scale'): reach the pirate ship 'The Talon' via Limestone Caverns (entered from the Statue/boulder puzzle: put lamp in candle holder + put green stone in left hand lights a boulder, push boulder reveals the cave); unlock/open the north cavern door with the bronze key (from the Eucalyptus funnel -> golden pellet -> dig depression with shovel -> metal box chain) -- this triggers a scripted one-way collapse into the Amphitheater and force-drops the adventurer's lamp + weather-worn raft (non-blocking: remaining areas are either naturally lit or reached by swimming). From the Amphitheater: down, northwest, north, northwest, southwest, southwest (squeeze through a small opening) reaches Oceanside Grotto; west, west swims the bay and climbs the rope ladder onto the Main Deck. Up to the Crow's Nest and 'tie etherian banner to pole' ties the Etherian Banner (obtained earlier from Gwenevere's jacket/bell/lion-statue/Forest-Temple chain, then combined with the glass stone crystal to open the Massive Temple Doors and reach the jolly roger, later shown to Princess Thalia via the Ezmarelda-token/guard/footman escort chain for the golden pellet + parchment) to the pole atop the mainmast -- disassembly (txd) confirms this is the BEST of three possible endings: tying the jolly roger there instead triggers a disastrous cannon-fire/shipwreck/imprisonment ending, and leaving no flag (or the flag of Castle Darinore) triggers a lesser, low-key reward ending; only the Etherian Banner triggers the full royal-ceremony celebration text used here. Down to Main Deck, south to the Captain's Cabin, take chest (pried from the rotting captain's arms), open chest, take jewel obtains the Fabled Jewel of the Etherians (a large ruby) -- disassembly confirms hoisting the anchor requires either possessing this jewel or having at least opened the chest. North back to Main Deck, 'hoist anchor' (NOT 'raise anchor', which is an unrecognised verb; 'pull anchor'/'hoist anchor'/'take anchor' all work once the chest condition is met -- otherwise they print 'You are suddenly overcome by a strange sensation that you should search the pirate's vessel a little while longer.'), then 'sail ship' (NOT 'sail', 'sail west', or 'west', which all fail/misparse) triggers the full authored victory epilogue ending in the banner '*** The adventure is won ***' followed by the RESTART/RESTORE/CREDITS/QUIT prompt -- confirmed via disassembly (routine at txd offset ~20244-20304) to be the singular win text in the game, gated only by this ending's specific combination (Etherian Banner tied + anchor hoisted + 'sail ship'), not reachable by score. 'sail ship' is the final input; no trailing move follows it. Deterministic replay verified twice with seed=1 (identical SHA-256 transcript hash both runs). Recommended guard for tools/replay_walkthrough.py's parse_terminal_text (not added here -- out of this session's owned-files scope): match '*** the adventure is won ***' together with a distinctive nearby phrase such as 'king sylvius, queen margarite, and princess thalia' or 'fabled jewel of the etherians' to avoid false positives on other games.

Solved by hand under Linux Jericho 3.3.1; the story has no RNG so it is fully deterministic (replays identically with or without seed=1). The shipped in-game HINTS were consulted (campaign policy permits shipped hints); no external walkthrough was used. Story MD5 07a9ac3fdb26818e24c1ca53e8e88571 (Release 6 / Serial 111109 / Inform 7 build 5Z71). The station Node 4 is a 2x2 compass grid (Fore/Aft x Starboard/Port); movement uses FORE/AFT/PORT/STARBOARD. SOLUTION SPINE: (1) TURN ON LIGHT, then PRY WRECKAGE WITH PRISE BAR to free the leg pinned in the struts [+1]. (2) Collect the two tools: the SCREWDRIVER is inside Suzan Harrison's empty spacesuit in the last sleeping rack (Aft/Starboard), the NOZZLE twists off the exercise bike's water line (Fore/Starboard). (3) UNSCREW PANEL at the pod door (Fore/Port) to expose ten power wires and, holding them, a STICK PAD (super-velcro). (4) Open the jagged wall COMPARTMENT near the pod: its momentary button is aft by the experiments, so hold it hands-free -- PUT STICK PAD ON BUTTON (bonds the nitrogen line's L-bend to the button so it can't slip), ATTACH NOZZLE TO LINE (focuses the jet so it presses hard enough), OPEN VALVE; the compartment then stays open and you TAKE LOGBOOK from it [+1]. (5) Follow Quintin's margin note in the logbook: DISCONNECT GREEN WIRE, DISCONNECT YELLOW WIRE, CONNECT WHITE-AND-RED WIRE TO RED WIRE restores backup power (PRESS BUTTON now opens the door only partway -- debris blocks it). (6) Reclaim the pad, PUT STICK PAD ON PRISE BAR, and GET CHAIN WITH PRISE BAR to fish the length of chain out of the floor crack [+1]. (7) Clear the debris with a bicycle winch (Archimedes): UNSCREW BICYCLE to fold it open (a small holed wheel on long pedal levers), TIE CHAIN TO SMALL WHEEL, TIE CHAIN TO DEBRIS, TURN PEDALS -- the chain winds taut and shatters the debris [+1]. (8) EVA for the external battery: the fore hatch is permanently warped shut, so re-rig the chain as a tether -- UNTIE CHAIN FROM SMALL WHEEL, at Aft/Port TIE CHAIN TO EXPERIMENTS (a bolted, won't-move anchor; the bike anchor is explicitly rejected and too short), then JUMP out the open jagged end; the tether snaps taut and you land on the exterior. UNSCREW BATTERY, go IN. (9) Full power: at the panel PLUG RED WIRE INTO BATTERY and PLUG WHITE-AND-RED WIRE INTO BATTERY (the two current-carrying leads that 'normally run to the power source'); the pod door then opens fully [+1]. (10) ENTER POD; the computer is password-locked -- TYPE PMQDSMSH ON TOUCH SCREEN (the crew initials in reverse rank order: Patricia Morrison, Quintin Davies, Simon Mahil, Suzan Harrison) powers up the pod [+1]; PRESS ESCAPE launches it and Suze's craft arrives to rescue you [+1] -> escape. Static evidence for the two non-obvious steps (confirmed via txd): the password literal is 'TYPE PMQDSMSH ON THE TOUCH SCREEN' (string S2205) and the tether success text 'a chain that runs from the experiments to your suit, forming a tether' (S1946). PARSER GUARD: this ending sets no Inform 'deadflag'/quit (it drops to the RESTART/RESTORE/QUIT menu), so Jericho's victory() stays False and get_max_score reports 0; a replay harness should classify the win on the banner string 'You have escaped Node 4' together with 'You have 8 points out of 8', not on env.victory().

Fyleet (Jonathan R. Partington, Cambridge Phoenix 1985; Inform 6 re-implementation v2.01). Full 600/600 win, solved by hand from the Z-code -- no walkthrough used. seed=1 is REQUIRED: the parrot magic word (ACHU), the secret circular chamber's true exit (E), the word the reborn phoenix squawks (RUNSETJD), the mirror and window-pane words (MAMMOTH / OOTTAT), the eight rabbit-warren directions, the hippogriff fare (80 groats), the postbox chant (1 = beef), the lavish chamber's word (GUDGEONS), the great-court staircase (S) and the magic-square question (red then blue = 24) are all drawn from the RNG. Engine: the score is recomputed every turn by a 74-entry ledger (routine @0xb450) worth 540, plus two 10-point globals (curing the wolf bite by swimming the river; escaping the lavish chamber), on top of a 10-point base. PRAY on the runed mat at the shrine of Hurgenpor requires ledger >= 540 and is what grants Hurgenpor's protection, so essentially every point must be banked first (this route reaches the ceiling, 570/600, before praying). Key discoveries: MAMOV <noun> is an undocumented in-game magic word that teleports you to that object's room -- it is the only way to leave the corridor/idol/temple pocket alive (the bell room kills you two turns after you enter it) and the only way to move a relic between the relic chambers, whose exits are barred while you carry anything. The wishing well grants exactly one wish for one treasure thrown in, so throw in the PARROT: the parrot magic word summons it back out of the well afterwards, making the sacrifice free, and the wish must be (G) feather-fall, the only way into Odulforg's cellar. Water is turned into wine by playing the accordion to Bacchus (after reading the squiggly papers), and that one bottle of wine buys the single stationary turn needed to pick up the war-helmet in the barrel room. The sword cycles pink/blue/green every 1-4 turns: blue kills the scarecrow, pink the man-eating weed, green beats the green knight. Other set pieces: giants throwing rocks (only the east-wall square is safe from both), the DEMNOS book removes one patrolling monk, the mystic monks then have to be walked out of phase, the stone column gates the chamber maze by axis, the sign gives the warren direction, the gargoyles are pacified by animating the scarecrow's remnants in front of them with the wand, the hippogriff fare is paid in balanced ternary (the two portal chambers flip the coins between adding and subtracting), Humpty Dumpty's fall must be broken by arriving under his wall on the exact turn, the onyx from Fairservice's grave is the 'Mnem-onyx' that stops you forgetting in the cavern of Mnem, and the relics of Pancras/Vitus/Tropez/Valentine must be matched to the railway, dancing, seaside and lovers rooms. Finally: enter the temple carrying the orb, shield, helmet and sword (each parries one horror), kill Zygmund, and answer the magic square (8 1 6 / 3 5 7 / 4 9 2, red then blue) with TWENTY FOUR. The port then prints '*** Invalid Meaning_LX value at action time ***' and one extra daemon tick appending the 599-point text: the win routine's return code is an unimplemented meaning in the Perl->Inform translation (the same artefact as in the sibling game Hamil). The 'You scored 600 points out of a maximum of 600!  Hail, mighty Hero!' banner is the authored terminal.

Hoist Sail for the Heliopause and Home (Andrew Plotkin, 2010, @party demoscene). A poetic solar-sailing game with no score and no Jericho binding. Win = the good ending '*** Home ***'. Sail mechanic has two axes: spread (raise/lower/hoist) = speed, and tautness (tighten/loosen) = coupling to the medium. In the Dark Reaches at partial (not full) spread, when a star 'catches your eye' you 'steer toward star' to descend into its system. Route (seed 11, 46 commands): leave Myrmidal, drop to partial spread, steer into a golden star -> gas giant -> 'take tissue' (iridescent cloth). Depart; a nebula demands 'loosen sail' to reach the Pulsar's Nest, where 'tighten sail' rides the beam into a Corridor; steer to a blue-white star -> planetoid -> 'take light' (liquid light). Depart and chase the neutrino flux across the Galactic Halo, matching sails to each region (raise in bubbles, tighten in radiation, lower in the maze/thicket, loosen in dense clouds) to reach the Brown Dwarf; steer to its frozen planet (Ice-World) and 'take tablets' (frozen-helium tablets). Departing, a red supergiant goes supernova and wrecks the ship (Darkness/adrift). Repair by sacrificing all three treasures: 'pour light' (illuminate the debris), 'fill compass with tablets' (refill the cracked compass), 'rig cloth' (new sails). Then 'hoist sail' + 'raise sail' races home before the subliming cloth-sails fail -> '*** Home ***'. Seed 11 is pinned because the discovery star-types are drawn from the Z-machine RNG. CLASSIFICATION: won (the good, treasures-found homecoming). NOTE: needs a central parse_terminal_text guard for '*** Home ***' (the game is Jericho-unsupported, so done/victory/score are all unavailable and the banner is the only terminal signal). Solution ends exactly on the 'raise sail' that prints '*** Home ***'.

notes: Midair Madness (Paul J. Furio, 2010 PAX East SpeedIF; Release 1, serial 100327, Inform v6.31). A scoreless (max_score=0) one-puzzle comedy: Uncle Doug has switched off the engines of his private jet and cast an Anti-Gravity spell, freezing the plane stationary tens of thousands of feet over the Great Plains; you must restore gravity so the autopilot can land it. GENUINE AUTHORED WIN: the final command 'gnillaf jet' prints 'You cast the Gnillaf spell on the jet plane. As Gravity once again takes hold, the autopilot kicks in, firing up the jet engines and guiding piloting the plane safely on to it's final destination at Boston's Logan International Airport. Uncle Doug calms down once he exits the plane, and is met by another extremely tall bearded man. "Steve!" ... *** You have won *** In that game you scored 0 out of a possible 0, in 12 turns.' followed by the standard Inform RESTART/RESTORE/QUIT end menu. (GNILLAF = FALLING spelled backwards; the GET LAMP in-flight movie and the two tall bearded authors 'Doug' and 'Steve' are jokes about Get Lamp / Steve Meretzky.) Three rooms, aft->fore = west->east: Rear Cabin (S) has a storage cabinet with three tinted bulbs (red, green, purple) and three arrow cards (left, straight, right); Forward Cabin has a refrigerator holding an 8.5x11 black-plastic film marked '450nm' (plus joke food); Cockpit (E) has Uncle Doug, a mechanical mouse with three business-card slots ('first','second','third'), and a black box (a mouse-shaped platform on top, a light-bulb socket on a gooseneck, a paper tray below, and an output chute). PUZZLE: the black box is a maze runner. Developing the film reveals the maze (put the black plastic in the tray and screw the purple bulb into the socket -> 'a developed film' whose imprinted image is a 5x5 maze: row1 *F* *, row2 *   *, row3 **S**, i.e. the mouse enters at S facing north and must reach F). From S the path is: go STRAIGHT (north) one cell, turn LEFT (west) one cell, turn RIGHT (north) into F -- so the arrow cards go straight->first slot, left->second slot, right->third slot. Placing the loaded mouse on the platform ('put mouse on platform') runs the maze; a correct solution rings a bell and drops a 'spell scroll' into the chute (a wrong order ejects the mouse instead). The scroll teaches the spell, and 'gnillaf jet' (directing the spell at the jet plane; a bare 'gnillaf' fails with 'Perhaps you need to direct the spell at something?') wins. Note: developing the film is only the intended *hint* for the card order; it is not mechanically required, so this minimal 12-command solution loads the cards directly and omits it. The win is seed-independent (no RNG on this path; three fresh Jericho runs at seed 1, seed 1 and no seed give the identical transcript hash); seed=1 is pinned only for convention. Jericho 3.3.1 reports done=False and victory()=False on the winning turn because the game shows the Inform end menu rather than issuing @quit and max_score is 0, so classification is by the authored '*** You have won ***' banner. Evidence: total_inputs=12, final_input='gnillaf jet', score 0/0, story SHA256 f883a3efb0df53338ee5be093c38ab988bf8ba32b37a1103f550a34a43a35424, transcript SHA256 a7dc67f23789da6b641d792f5492118f93e68715ca60b304499fb9bd58de64fd.

The game sets the standard Inform deadflag (global g14) to 2 exactly once, in routine r0291 (the north-exit of Second Class into First Class): test_attr 'first-class pin' #1a (the library 'worn' attribute) -> if the pin is being worn it prints string s162 (the Douglas Adams finale) and stores g14=2, printing the canonical '*** You have won ***' banner; otherwise it prints s163 ('...you must have a first-class pin.'). No title keypress is required (empty prelude); the game starts directly in the Waiting Area. Solution: (1) 'ask marvin about babel fish' -> Marvin gives you a babel fish and auto-plants it in your ear, so the green-blur waiter's gibberish ('Nomph whenz uf sa wovek skuer?') becomes intelligible. (2) 'say abrty to waiter' -> answer with the reservation number printed on your reservation card ('abrty'); this sets the entry flag g8a=1 (r0285), seating you third-class. (3) 'n' into the Third Class Area, 'e' into the Second Class Area where Zaphod Beeblebrox guards a first-class pin on his shirt and refuses to let you take it ('Get your stinking Earthling paws off me!'). (4) 'order pan galactic gargle blaster' -> the waiter (r0290, order verb #54) fetches the drink. (5) 'give blaster to zaphod' -> he gulps it and falls unconscious (s171). (6) 'take pin' -> 'You remove the pin from Zaphod and put it on yourself.' (s175) which sets the pin's worn attribute #1a. (7) 'n' into First Class -> the waiter waves you onward and you meet Douglas Adams as the Universe ends, firing the win. Nidus, by Adam Atkinson (AJFA1), Cambridge Phoenix 1986; this is the Phoenix v1.04 / Inform 6.33 translation 1.140416 (story SHA256 b162b285a8a3fa768e20abc10aa89ca3f48d678d99b50959b525f9c6486a80bd). Solved to completion: 250/250 with the authored KIWS ending ("The last of the spells binding the parts of the Chaos realm has been removed! The universe collapses in upon itself, and you find yourself standing in the ultra-secret KIWS HQ on your home plane..."). seed=1 pinned; two fresh replays are byte-identical. PRELUDE: the single input 'no' answers the pre-game question "Would you like some background information ?". ENGINE NOTE: the Phoenix ending terminates the interpreter instead of printing an Inform '*** You have won ***' banner or a 'play again' prompt, so Jericho/libfrotz's C step() never returns on the final input ('recite eedul'); all 288 preceding commands replay identically under Jericho, and the win itself is verified with dfrotz. Jericho's get_score()/get_max_score() also read 0 for this game (custom Inform score globals); the in-game 'score' verb reports 215/250 immediately before the last input and the win routine sets the score global to the maximum 250. SOLUTION OUTLINE. (1) Playroom: SW/W/NW from the start drops everything and traps you in a child's playroom; the book's rule is 'an odd number of playthings in each container, and no toys not in containers' with 'containers are not toys' -- nine toys cannot split into four odd parts, so nest the trunk inside the box (counts recurse) and hold bag/sack/box yourself, which tidies the room AND carries all nine toys out into the twilight room. (2) Museum: throw the weighted thread into the pearlpetual motion exhibit, wave the needle -> pearl necklace (+20). (3) Throw the necklace at the grunt of pigs ("casting pearls before swine") -- pigs flee, leaving pearls and a piglet. (4) The collector accepts exactly eight exhibits; giving him the flute teaches you to play it, and the seventh accepted gift makes him hand over the fiery flower. (5) Clean the black rod (a rusty star falls off: 'kirrrrrk'/'trekkk') -> the white Universal Translator. (6) Chaos: throw the column-mater (collimate), the ample-friar doll (amplify) and the lump of energy (lens: focus) into successive chaos rooms to extend the beam of light south. Walking into total chaos is survivable only while carrying the book of rules. Which chaos room you step in from selects where the rod translates you and where you are dumped seven turns later: CHAOS1 -> smoke-room / prison entrance, CHAOS2 -> cubical cavity / dark passage, CHAOS3 -> Hoog sugar-mine office / healer ante-room. The CHAOS3 trip is the only way to get the clay flute past the portal of life ('that which lives may pass'); in the Patagonian room PLAY FLUTE turns it into the Patagonian nose-vole, and INSERT VOLE lets you breathe. The portal destroys only the most recently taken non-living item per crossing, so carry a sacrificial item (here the toy chariot, later the can and the needle). (7) CHAOS2 trip: EAT HUMBUG ("Bah, humbug!") drives off the demon guard, the font appears, WASH ROBE turns the grubby robe into white satin. (8) CHAOS1 trip: grab the smoke can from the special-effects store, then step into Amalrik's audience chamber on the second-to-last turn of the translator countdown and speak the magic phrase BRUTISH TEAROOM (the graffiti acrostic 'Take Orthogonal Noetherian Kernel's Adjoint' is the decoy; the real phrase is the savage lettering in the tea-room, and the museum hintlet about 'extraction of informational content from the embellishments of public edifices' is the pointer) -- Amalrik's own lenticular bolt becomes your lens and you are flung to the prison entrance while your possessions land in the brutish tea-room; the fruit-bat makes that room survivable. (9) OPEN CAN in the bug room suffocates the insect; TAKE INSECT earns a hand sting whose swelling (11 turns) is the only thing that lets the too-big ring be worn. Wearing the ring, TOUCH DOOR disintegrates the adamantite door (+10); the ring is single-use per wearing, so reach the healer before the swelling bursts. (10) The dark creature in the cell must be relayed to the dark den: a lit torch in the same room as the creature is extinguished forever, you may make only two consecutive moves in darkness, and carrying the creature through a lit room puts that room out, so the torch is shuttled ahead as a floor lamp. The creatures reward you with the (luminous) talisman and open a tunnel east. (11) Lift: only one of the granite seal and the basalt plug can be open at a time, and closing either flips the cylinder up/down -- close granite, open/close/open basalt to arrive at the guard-room, where YUCCA LYPTOSE (what a badly-eared koala mishears as 'Eucalyptus') animates the koala, which shreds the demon Co'kherr; the resulting Co'kherr Koala is the collector's seventh gift. (12) Endgame: extend the last chaos leg with the lens, give the healed knight the white satin robe and then the Universal Translator -- she sweeps you into the Nidus, THROW TALISMAN implodes the radiating demon, JUMP reaches the eleven force-nodes. Each spell must be spoken with a verb that fits it and no verb may be reused (reuse is fatal), and casting a spell also annihilates every spell below it in a fixed cascade (EEDUL > POMYN > YUFTO/SERQE > GOMBE/HQXKF > MIQUE > NYZTH > MUNGLE/SNODE/LIIOK), so the order is forced: declare MUNGLE, cry SNODE, shout LIIOK, exclaim NYZTH, intone MIQUE (this opens the gate to the outer nodes), call GOMBE, yodel HQXKF, incant SERQE, sing YUFTO, murmur POMYN. With ten gone, the sixteenth node opens; WAVE FLOWER (a 'shelf-razing flower') burns the high shelf and EEDUL thuds down (+10); RECITE EEDUL destroys the last spell and wins.

The Acorn Court by Todd S. Murchison (1997), a one-room escape puzzle, solved to completion 30/30 with '*** You have won ***' (Jericho victory()=True, done=True). You are locked in a courtyard behind an iron gate with a keyhole. Solution chain: (1) pick up a tennis ball, aim the antique tennis-ball launching machine at the oak tree, load the ball and switch the machine on -- the ball knocks a shower of five green acorns out of the branches (+10). (2) Gather the acorns and the rusty tin pail, which has four bullet holes; plug all four holes with acorns so it becomes watertight. (3) At the crumbling well, crank the frayed rope up, tie the pail onto it, crank down to submerge it and crank back up: the plugged pail retains a pool of water with the hand-carved wooden key (left by a previous prisoner) floating in it -- otherwise the key would drain out through the holes. (4) Take the key (+20 -> 30), unlock the iron gate and open it to win. Terminal input is 'open gate'; no title-screen keypress is required (the room is shown at reset, so prelude is empty). seed=1 pinned; replayed twice from fresh FrotzEnv interpreters with byte-identical output. Story SHA256 7b13c904bf7608fa0de902ce7ecd5fcd0e026f293fc67baa87b99a35a3190c9e. Puzzle logic confirmed by static Z-string decode ('the acorns which you plugged the bucket with have held', 'a small object drain out through the holes with the water', 'A very small wooden key ... carved by hand ... by a previous prisoner').

Calliope: An Interactive Obtrusion by Jason McIntosh (Release 1 / Serial 991001 / Inform v6.15 / Library 6/7), 1999 IF Comp. Deterministic authored WIN: the final input 'make new game idea' prints 'You open a fresh window, and smile as the ideas -- no code, none of that yet, just raw, pure ideas -- start to fill the screen. ... *** You have won ***'. Non-scoring narrative game (score stays 0; Jericho get_max_score()=0 and victory()/done stay False on the standard RESTART/RESTORE/QUIT terminal, but the banner is the standard Inform deadflag=2 '*** You have won ***'). seed=1 is REQUIRED: the housefly's flight/landing is Z-machine RNG, so the win only reproduces under a pinned FrotzEnv seed (two fresh seed=1 replays are byte-identical; an unseeded/random run does not reproduce). No title prelude -- the intro prints on reset and the first real command is 'take manual'. Solution logic (found by play + a static Z-string dump of the story file; no external walkthrough): you are an exhausted programmer who can't finish a hopelessly buggy IF entry before the competition deadline. The housefly that eventually buzzes in IS the 'bug'. Shape the Inform Designer's Manual into a club ('roll manual') and swat the fly ('hit fly with manual'); killing the bug snaps you into a genre-parody dream, Mary's Apartment (the sitcom). Following the sitcom script by reading the flyswatter's label ('read flyswatter', 'Made in Peoria') plays your role, and you wake at the desk realising 'you actually might have a genuine new idea in your possession'. Developing that idea ('make new game idea' -> 'You open a fresh window...') is the muse Calliope's authored inspiration ending. The 24 'z' waits pass the sleep clock until the fly arrives (move 26); under seed=1 the first 'hit fly with manual' connects. Guard strings: roll manual, hit fly with manual, read flyswatter, make new game idea. Carnival by Admiral Jota (speedIF five and a half, 1999). You're at a carnival with one dollar, wanting to win a prize. The carnival is a shuffle maze: every movement 'deposits you elsewhere', so you cannot navigate deterministically -- but Jericho seeds the Z-machine RNG (pinned here to seed 12345), which makes the walk reproducible. The Game Booth has seven colored targets (red, blue, green, yellow, purple, black, white) and a sign: 'throw a rock at the right target and you win.' The game is deliberately rigged. The winning color (Game Booth property #29) starts unset (0) and is only assigned after enough turns elapse (a ~15-turn ambient-voice cycle); the periodic voice claiming a color 'is lucky' is a red herring and does NOT name the real winning target. The reliable tell is EXAMINE-ing any target, whose description ('The target is just a wooden circle colored X') reports the booth's true current winning color; that color does not re-randomize while you stand at the booth. Route: fifteen 'north's shuffle you to the Game Booth exactly when the winning color has just been set (seed 12345 -> yellow); take a rock from the counter, examine a target to confirm the color, then throw the rock at that colored target. 'As the rock hits the target, you hear a loud DING! ... Nice guess.' *** You have won *** Jericho does not bind this game (victory()/score disabled), so completion is detected from the standard closing banner. No title-screen keypress is needed (empty prelude).

The Cask (max score 31). Escape a wine-cellar prison. Wiring puzzle uses inverted 'light switch' logic: the ceiling wire is live, so the switch must be OFF to take it safely (stand on chair, take wire, +5), then ON to safely insert it into the machine's panel (put wire in panel, +3). Toggle the switch OFF again (button only works with switch off), then run the drum press: stand on chair, push button, wait 3 turns for the cover to open (+5), `up` to enter the drum (+3). Inside, a heavy cylinder crushes you within a few turns: open bundle, take rat, wrap the cloth (from the wire bundle) on the saw, cut the little hole into a big hole, then `enter hole` to drop back to the Wine Room. `search rat` reveals a golden key hidden inside the dead rat; `take key` (+5) extracts it WITHOUT destroying the rat (note `cut rat with saw` would shred the rat and lose the elephant scare). Go W to the Bare Room, unlock the steel door with the key, open it, W into the Small Garden where an elephant charges. `show rat to elephant` -> 'The elephant shrieks at the sight of the mouse, and run.' -> '*** You have won ***'. Win routine R0319 sets deadflag G14=#02 (the tsv banner_state columns Gef/04 are unreliable). show/present/give rat to elephant all win; `throw rat at elephant` fails ('you lack the nerve').

CHEATER by Daniel Schmidt is a deliberate META-puzzle: the in-game 'info'/hint text states it 'isn't a traditional IF puzzle' and 'you can only win by thinking like the main character and cheating' -- the title screen's version listing carries the Inform 'D' flag, meaning the DEBUG verbs are enabled, and the game's gratitude-for-debug-verbs paragraph is an explicit hint to use them. The Toaster of Battle Creek sits atop a smooth 30-foot pedestal that cannot be climbed; the obvious tools are traps (the ACME rocket pack explodes -> death; climbing/jumping down without a rope -> death, mirroring the dopey assistant Walter's 'faulty rope'). The intended solve is to CHEAT with the debug verbs: 'purloin toaster' teleports the toaster straight into your inventory, 'gonear walter' teleports you to the Entrance of Cave (where Walter waits), and 'north' (the cave exit) wins because the leave-routine checks the toaster is in your possession. Non-Jericho (score 0/0), so the win is detected via the '*** You have won ***' banner. Verified offline. Win confirmed via ztools txd disassembly: R0243 stores deadflag(G0c)=2 when leaving with the Toaster; R0237/R0242 store deadflag=1 (rocket-pack / fall deaths).

Cheer Up (Sam Barlow SpeedIF) - you are a fish. An unavoidable scripted intro (~15 turns of waiting) nets you and dumps you, unconscious, into the fish basket on the counter of The Kingfisher Fish And Chips Shop, guarded by Albert the Alligator and shared with Otto the Mouse. A Toys-R-Us Bag holding one rusty lead-painted metal bit sits out of reach overhead. FLAP ON the FISHSLICE twice: the second flap pushes its handle down so the blade rests on the counter as a catapult. WAIT until Otto potters onto the blade ('walking onto it'), then FLAP ON FISHSLICE again to launch him into the bag, knocking it into the basket (Albert delivers the required phrase 'thy gills are as unclean as a lobster's arse'). TAKE the BIT (into your mouth) and THROW BIT AT ALBERT: the alligator swallows the lead, combusts, and the blast flings you back to sea -- '*** You have won ***' (30/30, 'it was all a dream'). Seed 12345 pins Otto's wander timing; the fixed 4-turn wait catches him on the blade.

The Chicken Under the Window -- An Interactive Farce by Lucian Smith (SpeedIF Chicken Comp 1998), a parody of Andrew Plotkin's 'The Space Under the Window'. You don't act with verbs; you type words you SEE in the on-screen narrative and each accepted word morphs/extends that sentence (any other word answers 'That word is not near the narrative'). The opening sentence is 'The cars zoom by, so the chicken can't cross. ***'. Goal: grow the story until 'The chicken crosses.' (string s167), which sets deadflag and brings up the standard RESTART/RESTORE/UNDO/QUIT end prompt. This 8-word path follows the triumphant 'dance of freedom' branch (the chicken survives, rather than being hit by a truck): 'cars' -> 'an opening appears'; 'opening' -> 'The chicken darts into the traffic, cars surging left and right'; 'left' -> 'cars surging left, right, left, right,... A pattern begins to form'; 'form' -> the pattern names tires/wheels; 'artless' -> 'an artless dance' deepens to 'an endless hypnotic dance'; 'scream' -> 'screaming, singing wheels'; 'assimilat' -> 'Assimilating the dance, the chicken moves forward'; 'expressio' -> '...the self-expression freeing its inner chick into a joyous waltz of freedom,... The chicken crosses.' Win banner is the game's 'The chicken crosses.' (deadflag set; FrotzEnv.victory() stays False and the game enters its post-win RESTART/RESTORE/UNDO/QUIT menu, so done is reported False). Recognized as a win by adding 'the chicken crosses.' to parse_terminal_text in tools/replay_walkthrough.py. Verified via manual_solve/run.py and a full reachability BFS over the narrative-word graph (jericho).

Too Chicken to Make a Deal? — a Let's Make a Deal / Monty Hall parody. First 'cross dusty road' triggers the game-show intro (the chicken host speaks). Crossing the dusty road a second time = take the joke book = '*** You've settled for less ***' (a loss). The real win is to gamble correctly. 'lie down' runs R0262: SET_ATTR 'dusty road',#08 and prints the secret clue ('the tracks are elongated words: "Pick Road Two."'). After a few turns the chicken makes the three gamble roads appear (R0257, fires on a daemon ~3 waits later). With dusty-road attr#08 set, crossing Road Two awards the fixed prize value #07 (R0247), which sets G13=#02 -> the BEST ending S122: 'the Power to Make Money Selling Interactive Fiction' -> '*** You have won ***'. Without attr#08 the prize is random (G86), so reading the tracks first makes the win deterministic. Verified 3/3 (3 waits needed reproducibly on default seed) via manual_solve replay; classifies won (standard '*** You have won ***' banner).

THE LESSON OF THE CHICKEN (R. Noyes, 1998) - a body-swap puzzle solving 'why did the chicken cross the road?'. You start as farmer Wang Chung with a magic axe (inscribed 'Trade roles. Sever connections. Complete the circle.') and a chicken's head on the old stump. (1) 'examine blood' sets attr#09 on the 'splotches of blood', which opens the NW exit (R0249 returns room 24 only once the trail is discovered). Orpington (William J. Shlaer): a chicken-walking physics sim. Answer Sex?->yes, Are you female?->yes to become Buffy Orpington. Locomotion: legs are objects (right/left); a walking gait cycle is up<leg>/back<other>/down<other> repeated; "back <leg>" lurches forward ~10 units in the facing direction when the other foot is down, or slews (turns) when both feet are down. Turn by repeating back left/down left (each = +1 facing, CW). Flight: build speed by walking (gait=walking with momentum) then flap to take off; while flying you glide ~20 units/turn in the facing direction, fast enough to clear the road. The road is lethal (per-turn 1/8 pickup + 1/20 hawk death) so cross quickly. Solution: face NW and walk to the Gate (NW corner ~182 north/182 west), then repeatedly glide SOUTHWEST (rebuild speed + flap x3 per segment) across the road and down to The Nest at ~49 north/315 west. dark.z5 is 'Dead of Winter', Christina Pagniacci's SmoochieComp 2001 entry (Release 1 / Serial 010104, Inform 6.21). max_score=0 and Jericho never binds victory()/deadflag (the ending fires via a timed cutscene routine that ends in @quit inside a read_char loop), so completion is detected from the closing banner. Plot: the Ice Queen kidnapped your boyfriend Saul, leaving a blue crystal snowflake; she demands the 'Heart of Winter' (guarded by the Dragon) in exchange. The mirror in the Dragon's chamber reveals the Heart of Winter is YOU. Static analysis (ztools txd) of the talk-to-Queen action routine r0255 shows the ending branches on Saul's property #29 (hex; property 41, initial value 0): if it is < 0 you are frozen into a statue and shatter while Saul stays with the Queen (bad end, prints string s126); if it is >= 0 the Queen's magic rebounds and destroys her, Saul embraces you and you 'make your way home' (authored good end, prints s127 then the s128 newspaper epilogue revealing you both actually froze to death together -- a bittersweet reunion-in-death, the best of the two endings). Modifiers found in the disassembly: giving the blue crystal to the demon (r0259) subtracts 5; accepting the Dragon ('yes', r0271) subtracts 1; refusing the Dragon ('no') adds 1. Therefore the good ending requires crossing the Gorge of Despair WITHOUT paying the demon -- refuse it, fall to the branch, jump into the River of Storms, then wait three turns for its turn-counter (River prop #29) to reach 4 so the ice-bank exit opens (routine r0265) and go north -- and then refusing the Dragon (net Saul.#29 = +1 >= 0). The terminal move 'talk to queen' produces the winning banner ending '...you walk out of the cave, and make your way home.' (absent the statue/shatter text of the bad end). Deterministic: two fresh Jericho (3.3.1) replays produced identical transcript SHA256 0ebfe9ce69f3d68021d0c51762734ecc50f57db289b86cfc7be9f80107093812. The earlier solution reached only ~45-50/100 because it took the Voodoo Chicken Eggplant ending, which is NOT the maximum-score win. Disassembly (work/ztools .../txd) shows the score global G0d gets +5 (search shadows), +5 (search snam -> retrieve the Dr. Bronner's soap bottle from Snam's pockets), +20 (give gerbil to thrappy), +20 (run across Snam's bloated corpse), and a +50 award in routine R0415 reached only when you 'read bottle to nova' (G2c == object 107 = Doctor Nova): you recite Dr. Bronner's EUCALYPTUS 18-in-1 'Moral ABC' sermon at Nova, who repents. So the points the old path missed were (1) 'search snam' for the bottle and (2) using the soap SERMON ending instead of the eggplant. Puzzle chain: 'search shadows' finds the GERBIL pet (+5). 'search snam' takes the Dr. Bronner's soap bottle (+5). Doctor Nova's child brother Thrappy blocks the way north and 'wishes for a pet', so 'give gerbil to thrappy' clears him (+20). Drag Snam's body up room-by-room ('push snam north', only possible once Thrappy is gone). The catwalk over the novecilline vat drops a section, leaving an uncrossable gap; novecilline makes flesh bloat, so 'put snam in vat' so his bloating corpse fills the gap as a temporary bridge ('n' to run across, +20). In the Final Showdown, 'read bottle to nova' recites the soap-label sermon to Nova (+50) and wins. Do NOT pour the soap into the vat (that dilutes the novecilline -> only the 'swam away' escape ending) and do NOT throw the Voodoo Chicken Eggplant (that is the lower-scoring 'alchemist mack daddy' ending).

DEJA VU by Graham Nelson (1993 Inform demonstration). Deterministic MAX-SCORE checkpoint: 22/50, rank 'adventurer', 19 turns under Jericho 3.3.1 seed 1. A POSITIVE seed is mandatory: Jericho's FrotzEnv.seed() does `seed = seed or self.bindings.get('seed', -1)`, so a declared seed of 0 is falsy and silently degrades to the time-varying -1 -- the previously declared seed 0 did NOT pin this game's RNG (verified: two fresh processes at seed 0 give different transcript SHA256s; three fresh processes at seed 1 are byte-identical). Final banner: 'You have so far scored 22 out of a possible 50, in 19 turns, earning you the rank of adventurer.' Deadflag g08=0 (alive); done=False. WIN IS PROVABLY UNREACHABLE: the banner routine's 'You have won' branch requires deadflag g08==2, but all five g08 writers store #01 (death) -- grenade blast, step into darkness, dive/drown in reservoir, shoot self, shoot the aged snake -- and there is no store #02, no inc/dec, and no indirect storew/storeb into the deadflag word; the win banner is dead code. Scoring (global g01) has exactly two award sites, both gated on attribute #19 (=25 dec): +5 first-visit to an attr#25 room, +4 first-take of an attr#25 object; no set_attr#19 exists so the set is static. The six attr#25 entities: Reservoir (+5), West End of Hall of Mists (+5), platinum bar (+4), ray gun (+4), sack cube obj30 (+4) -- all collected here -- and the Y2-rock cube obj16 (+4) which is UNOBTAINABLE: its before-routine (r0100) unconditionally intercepts the Take action with 'You flinch from touching the cube, which is white hot!' (no temperature var / timer / attribute gate; verified empirically by isolating it), so its +4 can never be scored. Hence 22 is the hard maximum; the 'out of a possible 50' is a hardcoded string literal, not a computed cap. This is +4 over the prior 18/50 baseline (adds sack cube obj30). Route notes: three cubes share the name 'featureless white cube', so the starting-held cube19 is dropped in the Y2 Rock Room (cmd 1) to keep the later 'take cube' at the sack unambiguous; the carry limit is 5 held items (the take routine r20c2 refuses only when MORE than 4 are already held), so the two 'drop' commands are slack rather than necessity -- a 17-command variant without them reaches the identical 22/50; 'echo' stills the Loud Room acoustics so the bar is takeable; 'shoot snake' ages the snake so West End can be entered (the clover is NOT required, confirmed). Determinism: score and deadflag are identical on every replay and at every seed (always 22 / 0); only the game's random atmospheric one-liners vary, and they come from the Z-machine RNG, so byte-identical transcripts require a POSITIVE Jericho seed -- verified byte-identical across three fresh processes at seed=1 (and at seed=12345), and verified NON-reproducible at seed=0. Final 'score' is a meta command (no state change); last score-affecting command is 'w' into West End. Map completeness (previously under-reported): the world is 10 rooms -- Y2 Rock Room, Reservoir, Loud Room, Broken Passage, Window (UP from Broken Passage, holds the iron key), Yellow River Rock, Debris, Hall of Mists, West End, and Canyon Ledge. Canyon Ledge sits behind the locked iron door (obj26, door_to=27, with_key=obj24) and is UNREACHABLE: the only unlocker is action 0x16 ('unlock/open NOUN with HELD'), and this 1993 library's parser cannot match that grammar line -- 'unlock door with key' returns 'I didn't understand that sentence' and 'open door with key' returns 'I only understood you as far as wanting to open the iron door', reproduced identically under dfrotz, so it is a shipped game bug, not a harness artifact. It costs nothing: Canyon Ledge has no attribute 25 and no contents. story_sha256=64bb01746966c2280185a56aa6e641b65fe0353dc28a2ac1b178194aad25e006 ; at seed=1: game-text transcript_sha256=75658dd4d0fafe115d36b810f004ae7eab48f0ab409169675b8acf7f4e664bbe ; audit transcript_sha256 (tools/manual_walkthrough_batch write_transcript format)=fcbe39bea27441ea31df870c017a0370293e3848548ddc47675ff6e411366568.

Basket of Destiny by John Cater (SpeedIF 15, 2001), an intentionally short comedy game with no scoring (max_score=0). Solved to its authored winning terminal '*** You have won ***'. Because the game is not Jericho-bound, victory()/done stay False and score detection is disabled; the win is established from the exact authored banner plus the terminal RESTART/RESTORE/QUIT menu (a following empty input yields 'Please give one of the answers above', proving the end state). Goal: finish your Underwater Basketweaving homework, then get into the TV studio taping. Solution: go west to the bedroom and 'look under mattress' to recover the stashed basketweaving reeds; the reeds must be soaked before they weave, and the bathtub drains unless plugged, so take the stopper from the kitchen sink, put it in the tub drain, turn on the faucet to fill the tub, drop the reeds in and 'weave reeds' -> 'You adroitly weave the reeds into a passable basket. Huzzah, a success!'. Then in the kitchen 'search papers' finds the invitation and auto-transports you to Front of the Studio, where a cardboard cutout of Graham Nelson blocks the entrance holding out its hand ('you can't go in unless you're invited'); 'give invitation to cutout' places the invite in its hand, and 'e' triggers the win: 'The cardboard cutout of Graham Nelson somehow slides aside, allowing you to move unimpeded into your new life as ace underwater basketweaver and star of the hit show...'. Terminal-producing input is 'e' (14th command, no trailing gameplay); no title-screen keypress required (room shown at reset, prelude empty). seed=1 pinned; puzzle fully deterministic (no RNG). Replayed twice from fresh FrotzEnv interpreters with byte-identical output. Story SHA256 96ecd9f0faafbb0afed7589c9c31e0f35423965c9eec7ca34638f47edd349bc1. Winning text confirmed independently via static Z-string decode (manual_solve/sessions/zdump.py).

Destruct (SpeedIF, Agent Orange vs. Dr. Letterman's world-destroyer). No score; win = disabling the doomsday machine. From the Complex entrance go 'down' into the Entry maze. The airdropped satellite map's directions (N,W,S,N,D) are a deliberate trap: 'n','w','s' misdirects you into a pit-needle and you're captured, waking stripped of possessions in an 'Easily-escaped prison cell'. 'open grille' + 'e' reaches the Ventilation shaft; 'east' tumbles you down through a grating into Dr. Letterman's coffee bar; 'north' to the Spacecraft hangar; 'down' through the manhole to 'Amidst the diabolical machine', where a frizzly-haired man works with his back to you. Do NOT attack him (action attack -> deadflag G13=4 -> '*** BOOM! ***', the machine detonates and kills you) and do NOT push the spacecraft's red button (action push -> G13=3 -> '*** The galaxy is your oyster ***', you flee as Earth explodes = mission failed). Instead TALK to him: 'ask man about machine' (answer/tell/ask all trigger the man's life routine R0263, action set #51/#52/#53 -> STORE G13,#05). He turns out to be H.G. Wells, who helps you disable the contraption -> '*** You'll never see him again ***' (Dr. Letterman escaped in Wells's ship). This is the game's success ending: deadflag G13=5 prints the custom banner via R0264 (the standard 'You have won' at G13=2 is never written; win-banner detection was a false positive, but disabling the world-destroyer is the intended victory). Found via txd: R0263 gates action #42(attack)->G13=4 vs #51/#52/#53(talk)->G13=5; R0264 maps G13 3/4/5 to 'galaxy is your oyster'/'BOOM!'/'You'll never see him again'. Deterministic, 10 cmds, seedless.

A Bear's Night Out? No -- 'Dewdrops on the Petals' by Papillon (a metatheatrical one-act play). Deadflag win, no score-cap gate. You are an actor who must play three roles by changing costume BACKSTAGE: the cloth worn = the cloak of the hero Captain Maurice (carrying the stick makes it his sword, the board his shield); the petticoat worn = the wizard McFaud. Follow the game's own built-in blow-by-blow walkthrough (HELP menu strings S513-S545): (1) As the hero go onstage and DROP the board -- it becomes a 'trapdoor' (this is theatre, it needn't be real); OPEN it (+1) and go DOWN. (2) Beneath the stage a demon is bound by a sandbag out of reach; as the hero (cloak + sword) CUT SANDBAG WITH SWORD to free him -- you are hauled back onstage. (3) Summon him: go offstage, WEAR PETTICOAT (keep the cloak on so you are still the wizard-hero), go onstage and OPEN TRAPDOOR -- the demon erupts and the scene changes to the Walls of Paris. (4) Signal for help by making a flag: the cloak only serves as flag-cloth when NOT worn, so offstage TAKE OFF CLOAK (+1, you snap into the wizard role via the petticoat), TIE CLOTH TO STAFF to build a flag, go onstage and WAVE FLAG -- the extras swarm, Paris is saved and *** You have won ***. Seed-independent; no prelude keypresses (the title screen accepts the first command directly).

Dino Hunt: A Prehistoric Safari (Admiral Jota, 2000), score 4/4. You are a kid at a four-room playground -- Sand Box (centre), Basketball Hoop (N), Swing Set (E), Slide (W) -- who wants to play with three toy dinosaurs that are hidden around the playground. Each dinosaur is off-stage until you perform the right action, which also scores +1: (1) 'dig sand' in the Sand Box uncovers the tyrannosaurus rex (R0274 action #38 dig -> INSERT rex, S140); 'take rex'. (2) Go 'w' to the Slide and 'search grass' -- the overgrown grass under the slide hides the brontosaurus (R0279 action #22 examine -> INSERT bronto, S152); 'take bronto'. (3) The pterodactyl is stuck up in the basketball net: the basketball starts at the Swing Set, so go 'e', 'take ball', then 'n' to the Basketball Hoop and 'shoot hoop'. Each shot bounces the ball back onto the floor (routine near R0289 increments the hoop's prop #29: S171 backboard/S172 rim/S173 backboard+rim), so 'take ball' between attempts; the 4th shot (count 4) swishes through and knocks the pterodactyl out of the net (S174/S175); 'take pterodactyl'. Finally return 's' to the Sand Box holding all three dinosaurs and 'play with rex' -- the win routine R0273 (action #5e 'play') checks that tyrannosaurus rex, brontosaurus and pterodactyl are each in the room or carried, sets G14=2 (deadflag) and prints S133 -> '*** You have won ***' (4/4). Path/mechanics reverse-engineered via txd -g (reveal routines R0274/R0279, hoop counter, win gate R0273) + infodump object tree (dinos + basketball parented off-stage/Swing Set). Deterministic, 18 cmds, seedless.

Why did the Dino cross the Road? by Richard Bos (Dino-comp / SpeedIF, 2000). You are a hungry dinosaur; a small white chicken across a busy transcontinental road is the only food in sight, and a mysterious 'growling noise' (your empty stomach) plagues you. 'step on car' (verb #5f = break/step-on) crushes a passing red convertible, whose debris jams the road so all traffic grinds to a halt. Now you can cross: 'n' to the Other Side (the chicken flees back across to your original Side of Road), 's' back to the Side of Road (the chicken flutters south to the Small Clearing), 's' into the Small Clearing where it finally settles down to peck. 'take chicken' pins it under your toe and picks it up (chicken handler R0253, action #0f); 'eat chicken' (action #2b, chicken held) -> R0253 sets deadflag=2 -> '*** You have won ***' (2/2), and you get discovered by a monster-movie film crew. Standard Inform victory banner (already matched). NB: the naive chase kills you (following the lure into the jungle = deadflag=1); the winning route reaches the clearing exactly as the chicken settles. Deterministic, 6 cmds.

DEADLINE (Or, Being Douglas Adams) by Gunther Schmidl, a SpeedIF joke game. You are Douglas Adams soaking in a bathtub while the phone (a looming deadline) rings ever more insistently. notes: The Zuni Doll by Jesse Burneko (1998), a survival-horror one-act, solved to completion 60/60 with '*** You have won *** ... earning you the rank of Zuni Slayer' (final input 'turn on disposal'). NOTE: Jericho cannot read this game's score global (get_score/get_max_score return 0 and victory() returns False); the win is authoritative via the terminal banner '*** You have won ***' plus the status line 'scored 60 out of a possible 60'. Story: your cat Elmo knocks the gold Talisman off the animate Zuni fetish doll under your bed; the flat is sealed (front-door deadbolt cut off). Solution chain: (1) Take the sheet; 'get up' triggers the scripted disaster (lamp shatters into glass shards, Elmo steals the Talisman, doll grapples). 'attack doll' breaks the grapple; 'cover doll with sheet' (the only object that occupies the doll) buys a lead to flee 'south' into the dead-end Bathroom. (2) 'close door' then 'lock door' -- a LOCKED bathroom door makes the doll slash through slowly over ~6 turns (an unlocked one it opens instantly for a one-shot kill); use that window to grab the slippers and, from the medicine cabinet, the hairspray and dental floss, and build a blow-torch: 'tie floss to lighter', 'tie lighter to hairspray', 'light lighter'. As the door gives way, 'spray hairspray at doll' engulfs it -- it 'runs flaming from the room' (single hairspray charge). (3) Wear the slippers (needed to cross the fixed glass shards that block 'east' while barefoot), unlock/open the door and go north then east into the Living Room and east to the Kitchen; 'open freezer' and 'take knife'. (4) THE KEY INSIGHT (found by disassembling the doll's daemon): torching the doll sets attribute 31 which disables its chase, so it 'camps' in the Living Room. The only thing that clears attr 31 is the doll picking up the French knife. Return west and 'throw knife at doll' -- it takes the knife as a 'superior weapon' (re-enabling its chase) and discards its small sword. (5) Immediately go 'east': 'The Zuni Doll chases after you!' into the Kitchen, where it 'leaps up onto the kitchen counter'; wait two turns and it 'leaps from the counter top... landing inside the open freezer'; 'close freezer' traps it (+5). (6) With the doll contained, go west and pick the desk drawer open with the doll's dropped small sword ('take sword'; 'unlock drawer with sword' -- 'a hard twist... a springy snap'); take the shiny key and rubber band; 'unlock cabinet with shiny key' for the ceremonial bell and divining rod. (7) Retrieve the Talisman from Elmo: 'untie tie' (from the bathrobe), 'tie tie to bell', 'ring bell' -- 'Elmo dashes out from under the sofa. He drops the little Talisman at our feet' -- then 'take talisman'. (8) Build the slingshot: 'attach rubber band to divining rod' (stretch it across the Y), 'load divining rod with talisman'. (9) Return east, 'open freezer' to release the doll, and 'fire divining rod at doll' -- 'Just as the Zuni Doll leaps, you let go! The Talisman... wraps around the Zuni Doll's neck... falls lifeless to the ground.' (10) 'take doll', 'put doll in disposal', 'turn on disposal' -- the doll is ground up, you go to bed with Elmo, and win 60/60. Terminal input is 'turn on disposal'; no title-screen keypress is required (the game opens in the Bedroom, so prelude is empty). seed=1 pinned for a byte-identical transcript, but the route is NOT seed-dependent (verified winning under seeds 0/1/2/5). Replayed twice from fresh FrotzEnv interpreters with byte-identical output. Story SHA256 28d5d7afd266adc82be320327a14ce1dbccd5437ce1597ce2c0b1618f0714f9c; transcript SHA256 eaa89fcb0ad7fbacdb64dfac0f402f9770979f085f8c6573302509c570747d7c. The knife->sword->desk and knife->clear-attr-31->chase mechanics were confirmed by static Z-code disassembly of the doll's per-turn daemon (obj 46; the chase moves the doll toward the player only when its state prop==2 AND attr 31 is clear; the freezer trap fires when the doll's parent is the Kitchen counter and the freezer is open).

Verified by replay from scratch under seed=1 (byte-identical across 2 replays). Reaches the genuine authored victory terminal: banner "*** You're rich beyond your wildest dreams and live a quite and comfortable life for the rest of your ill-begotten days. ***", followed by "In that game you scored 77 out of a possible 85, in 242 turns." and the RESTART/RESTORE/QUIT game-over prompt. Per txd, the endgame banner routine R0285 prints victory string S139 iff the deadflag global G14==6. Jericho does not support this game (get_score/get_max_score/victory/game_over all report 0/False), so correctness is read from the game's own status line (Score: 77 Moves: 242) and the printed banner, not from run.py's reward/done. Route summary: (Borphee north bank) take lantern; museum replica->georboz eyeglasses for Darkworld night-vision; refill Zn coin at Pheebor Junction; order bottled beer (bartender drops empty bottle down the chute to the Tavern cellar). Cross the One River via the hungus ride + raise the drawbridge (turn wheel). Traverse the vanishing forest path to the Dead End and descend the Black Hole into the grue-infested Darkworld. Darkworld navigation rule: at most 2 dark moves then 'light lantern' (scares grues, drops you into the lit real-world overlay) then 'turn off lantern' (returns to the tunnel, resets the ~2-move grue budget). Collect the chrome time sphere (IST Vault, open case + take sphere), the broadsword (Round Chamber) and the empty bottle (Tavern cellar), then climb back up to the Dead End. In the south forest fill the bottle with fresh water at the Pond, pick wildflowers at the Meadow and 'put bouquet in bottle' to keep them fresh. Re-descend, give the fresh bouquet to Esias (his rhyme reveals the magic word), reach the Grue Shrine and say 'plugh' to transform the Darkworld into Hades, take the brass shield in the Field of Souls (do NOT enter the Circle of Fire / Halls of the Dead / Gates directly -- all instant death). Exit Hades back to the Dead End, cross to the real-world South Beach by cutting the undergrowth east of the Clearing with the sword, enter the Cave and descend to the lava. Cross the lava river using the brass shield as a raft ('put shield on lava', 'get on shield', 's', 'u'), climb to the Rotting Tunnel and into the Demon's Lair. There, arm the time sphere by pressing its five colored buttons in interlock order blue,green,black,yellow,red (freezes the Demon), then 'cut chain with sword' and 'take amulet' -> victory. Score is 77/85; the remaining 8 points are optional side treasures (brass disk, scrap of paper, etc.) that are not required for the authored win.

Map: Office -w-> Hallway (-n-> Electrical Closet, -s-> Stairs 3rd) ; Stairs 3rd -d-> 2nd -d-> Ground; Ground -s-> Parking Lot. Puzzle: the Electrical Closet holds a squirt gun sitting between electrodes at 'a jillion volts'. Taking the gun makes a monkey-man drop down in front of the door and block you in ('The monkey-man prevents you from leaving.'). Firing the water-filled squirt gun at him ('fire gun at monkey-man') squirts water at his feet, bridging the electrodes to live flesh and vaporizing him -- this also discharges the electrified doorknob that otherwise blocks the Ground-level south exit with a mimesis-breaking 'mild shock' joke (routine r0290/string s150). With the monkey-man gone and the electrodes shorted, walk out: s (Hallway), s (Stairs 3rd), d, d (Ground), s (Parking Lot) -> win. The rest of the building (a filler hallway, a 'very large room' with Schrodinger's-bear cage and a Kirk/Shatner/beret gag) is optional SpeedIF flavour and not required. The Fluid of Life by Carl Muckenhoupt for SpeedIF Jacket 3 (Release 1 / serial 050828 / Inform v6.30). Full authored WIN: terminal banner '*** You have won ***' followed by the standard 'Would you like to RESTART, RESTORE a saved game or QUIT?' menu, printed on the final 'drink bottles' input. max score is 0 (the game has no scoring), so the win is a pure deadflag/terminal ending. IMPORTANT Jericho behaviour: for this game Jericho's env.victory() and step-done both remain False even at the win screen (a documented quirk noted in tools/manual_walkthrough_batch.py: with no built-in walkthrough victory() always returns False); the repo classifier still resolves this to 'won' because parse_terminal_text matches the '*** You have won ***' banner in the terminal observation. Route/plot: you begin head-down in the bay, drowning ('you've got seconds to live'). (1) 'up' -- struggle upward and clamber out onto the pier (The Waterfront). (2) 'south' to the Alley; 'search garbage can' three times to pull out a banana peel, a watermelon rind, and finally the WATER PISTOL (the garbage yields one item per search, in that fixed order; the banana peel and watermelon rind are red herrings). Your trenchcoat already holds a soggy note reading 'squirt bogey in the eyes'. (3) 'north' back to The Waterfront where a snarling watchdog guards the clinic; 'squirt watchdog with water pistol' -- 'Bull's-eye! ... It looks confused for a moment, then scrams. (Hydrophobia, perhaps?)'. (4) 'north' into the Homeopathic Clinic (a moonshine front: a still and bottles of 'pure distilled water. Or possibly completed homeopathic remedies'). (5) 'drink bottles' -- first drink uncorks a bottle and reveals the alcohol ('the clinic is just a front for a moonshine operation!'); (6) 'drink bottles' again -- 'You take a slug ... it sure makes you feel better. Freedom (anonymous / Kazuki Mishima, 2008 IFComp; Release 0, serial 080929, Inform v6.21). A scoreless (max_score=0) empathy piece designed, per its own Author's Note, 'to create the experience of suffering from social anxiety disorder' -- everyone yells at you, cashiers sneer, drivers won't stop, and it is held to Andrew Plotkin's Merciful standard so it is impossible to actually lose. GENUINE AUTHORED WIN: the final command 'hug woman' (hugging the lone nervous young woman in the inner College Conference Room) prints 'You give the young woman a hug. She looks surprised and trembles, then sighs and relaxes, closing her eyes. *** You have won *** In that game you scored 0 out of a possible 0, in 28 turns.' followed by the standard Inform RESTART/RESTORE/QUIT end menu. This exactly matches the game's own embedded WALKTHROUGH (get list; leave apartment; find the Market; get groceries; enter the automated checkout line; buy groceries; take the groceries back to your apartment and leave them there; push the crosswalk button and go west as fast as possible; enter the bookstore; examine the books; leave and enter the college building; find the girl and give her a hug). Map: Apartment <-s/n-> Hallway <-w-> Sidewalk SE <-n-> Sidewalk NE <-e-> Market; a 4-lane road (Road Far East/Mid East/Center/Mid West) crossed westward via the crosswalk (push button, then move west; the light turns green as you reach the far side) to Sidewalk NW (w = College Conference Room, s = Sidewalk SW -> w = Bookstore). Key constraints that force the order: you cannot carry groceries into the Bookstore or the College ('You probably shouldn't be wandering in there with your groceries') and cannot drop them on the street, so the groceries must be bought and dropped back at the apartment before the two west-side errands; the automated checkout line avoids the hostile human cashiers (the normal line also completes the purchase, but automated is the authored choice and fits the theme). Examining the books reveals the awaited book 'hasn't come in'. The win is seed-independent: the only RNG in the game is the cashiers' random insults, which the automated-checkout path never triggers, so the transcript is byte-identical with or without a seed; seed=1 is pinned only for convention. Jericho 3.3.1 reports done=False and victory()=False on the winning turn because the game shows the Inform end menu rather than issuing @quit and max_score is 0, so classification is by the authored '*** You have won ***' banner. Evidence (three fresh Jericho 3.3.1 interpreters -- seed 1, seed 1, and no seed -- byte-identical): total_inputs=28, final_input='hug woman', score 0/0, story SHA256 bf5b19be0268d83d7006682b976fd4bfe2651986209e3a5818bec32866f2dc17, transcript SHA256 7155f8d2376dcec7aa71498911401afe3f6255d33c374315b7b959ec3fb950f2.

Guess The Verb! (Leonard Richardson, 2000). BEST authored win: *** You have won all the prizes *** (guessed 5 verbs, completed 0 scenarios, 9 moves) -- deadflag G15=#06 (txd STORE G15,#06 at guess.txd:11636; win printed by R0280). Mechanic: flip the blue switch behind the booth so Lalrry ignores the 'shiny' adjective and accepts the tarnished quarter; pay once, then GUESS the verb the wheel lands on. A correct guess removes that verb from the wheel and lets you guess again WITHOUT paying, so guessing every result correctly cleans out all five prizes. The wheel result is RNG-driven and independent of the guessed word, so seed=1 is REQUIRED and pins the deterministic order RECONFIGURE, UNDO, DISEMBARK, SCRUTINIZE, FASTEN. Replayed twice from scratch (identical). 'Life on Gue Street' (a.k.a. guestret) -- a choose-your-path Zork parody. Each prompt reads 'Type "1" to continue, "2" to turn back, or "No" to take a different path.' Disassembly (txd R0005/R0006/R0007) shows a hidden progress counter G00: every '1' increments it, and the ENDING routine R0004 fires when G00 reaches 11. R0004 draws a single RANDOM #05 (the only RNG consumed during play -- all other randoms are spent in the R0003 startup deck-shuffle) and selects one of five endings: values 1-3 are the death vignettes (S003 thief/S004 grue/S005 coal-gas), values 4-5 are the WIN (S006/S007: 'you put the platinum bar in the case ... look for the entrance to the barrow, and your next adventure...'). Because the draw is fully determined by the post-shuffle RNG state, the ending is fixed per FrotzEnv seed. seed=1 lands on the winning ending: the 11th '1' (G00 reaches 11) prints the platinum-bar / next-adventure victory text. Reproducible only when pinned to seed=1.

henry.z5 = 'Finding Henry' by Duncan Cross (SpeedIF Leather, 3rd Anniversary). You must rescue Henry from a cave guarded by John Cerberus, who refuses anyone carrying a visible light source. Map: Mediterranean Beach (center); east -> Outside Large Hut (north -> House o' Leather shop with the prosthetic leather nose); from the hut, east -> Maize Maze; from the beach, west -> At Cave Mouth (north -> the guarded cave). Route: from the beach go 'east','north' to the shop, 'take nose','wear nose', 'south' back, then 'east' into the maze. The maze hands you a glowstick at random ('you trip over a glowstick'); it trips within a handful of 'east' moves, so the solution wanders 'east' ~20 times (trip verified for every tested RNG state, no death) and a single 'west' always exits the maze back to Outside Large Hut regardless of position. Go 'west','west' to the beach then Cave Mouth -- but the guard blocks a bare glowstick, so 'remove nose','put glowstick in nose','wear nose' hides the light inside the leather nose and 'north' lets the guard nod you through; you fall down a shaft into 'Almost Darkness' and the nose is ripped off. 'take glowstick','north' approaches an eerie glowing face that turns out to be a candle in a pumpkin; 'examine pumpkin' then 'open pumpkin' reveals the candle is dynamite with a near-spent fuse -- you drop the glowstick in and dive for cover ('[Press any key.]', dismissed by the 'wait' command), the blast opens a wall in the Sticky Cave, and 'north' reaches the Hidden Cave where Henry is 'alive and well' -> '*** Happy 3rd Anniversary, SpeedIF! ***'. Jericho-unsupported (victory() disabled, score 0/0); seed 1 pins the maze glowstick RNG, and the win is detected via the 'Happy 3rd Anniversary, SpeedIF!' banner added to replay_walkthrough.parse_terminal_text. Map/strings and guard light-source rule confirmed via play + z-string disassembly; the keypress after 'open pumpkin' is not in the batch tool's auto-drain markers, so an explicit filler command ('wait') consumes it.

Seed 1, 36 commands; the final input 'sleep' prints the authored terminal banner '*** Pleasant dreams! ***' at score 35 out of a possible 40 in 36 turns. You are a house hippo (tiny cat-like creature); the intro sets three drives -- escape the scary Halloween sounds, grab a snack, and nap in your sock nest. Seven scored achievements fire (+5 each): (1) comfort the crying dragon under the table by giving it the crumpled paper napkin taken from the window ledge (reached via 'climb web'); (2) reach the treat table -- the tablecloth is too slippery until your feet are sticky, so eat the sticky lollipop the dragon leaves behind, then 'climb fabric' (walking up sticky-footed); (3) eat a treat ('eat cookie'); (4) get rid of the box of scary sounds -- step on its button to silence it three times, waiting ~3 turns each time so the annoyed vampire keeps re-enabling it until he finally 'walks off with it'; (5) escape the spider -- from the top of the apple basket on the cold porch, throw the shiny red apple at the spider (a costumed house cat), which overturns the basket; hide in the jack o' lantern so the owner ('a black cat walking on two legs') comes out and carries the spider away; (6) plug your ears with the wad of cotton pulled from the soft spiderweb ('pull web'), so the noise can't keep you awake; (7) return to the nest under the sofa ('enter sofa') and 'sleep' -- the win. The hippo can carry only one item at a time. Terminal proof via RAM globals (global table from header 0x0C): score global G03 = 35 = does not equal max global G01 = 40; turn global G04 = 36; and the deadflag global at index 23 (G17) flips 0 -> 1 on the final 'sleep'. The remaining 5 points (max 40) come from an 8th point-source that could not be obtained in the same playthrough: two exhaustive automated score-delta probes (fresh hubs + the full pre-sleep state) and a full disassembly (Jericho _disassemble_game) score-flag inspection found no additional single action that raises G03 beyond these seven events, indicating the missing achievement is a mutually-exclusive alternate branch (e.g. an alternate use of the single napkin) rather than an additional obtainable reward; 35/40 is the practical single-run maximum that still reaches the authored victory, and is a genuine win (historical automation for this title reached only a loss). PARSER GUARD NEEDED (central tools/replay_walkthrough.py parse_terminal_text, NOT edited here per ownership): register a 'won' rule for '*** pleasant dreams! ***' guarded by 'you scored 35 out of a possible 40' and/or the story line 'you snuggle up in your nest of socks and fall fast asleep'.
