H.R.S. (a satirical job-interview SpeedIF) is a pure multiple-choice game with no parser grammar (0 verb entries): every turn is answered by typing an option number. Four hidden aptitude stats -- Technical, Leadership, Teamwork and Salary (globals G02..G05) -- all start at 2, and after EVERY one of the nine questions the game fails you ('The phone never ring') the instant any stat drops to 0 or below. The winning answers keep all four positive throughout: (1) use goto? -> 1 Nope; (2) if you must, how? -> 1 Infinite Loop; (3) leaderless group -> 1 Lead; (4) can you do the project? -> 5 'if this way... if that way...'; (5) project behind schedule -> 2 Do your best; (6) Bob is a loser -> 2 Help him; (7) most important trait -> 2 Skills; (8) work nights/weekends -> 3 Do I get overtime?; (9) low pay offer -> 1 'Make me an offer' (the only closing answer that reaches the win check). Final stats 5/4/4/4 -> the interviewer shakes your hand: 'Congratulations! When can you start?' (report card Technical A, Leadership B, Teamwork B, Salary $50,000/year). inhumane.z5 is 'Inhumane: An Infralogic Massacre' by Andrew Plotkin (Revision 2 / Serial 31415926 / Inform v1405, a parody of Infocom's Infidel). max_score=90. The authored win is NOT to avoid the traps but the opposite: a voice (the dungeon master) offers a deal -- 'get yourself killed by every single one of my deathtraps, after getting as far towards solving it as possible, then I will give up and let you take the coffin.' There are 9 scored deathtraps (10 pts each). Death does NOT end the game; you respawn in the Round Room and the world resets, so all 9 correct deaths are chained in one run. Each trap must be reached and triggered in its 'maximal' way (a premature/wrong death gives g01=0, 'that hardly counts'). The 9 traps: (1) board the swinging platform over the 65ft pit, then ride it until the invisible northeast bar sweeps you off; (2) unlock the chest to release coal gas then open the spring door so its steel knob sparks on the flint wall; (3) reach the North Stalagmite Room (breaking stalagmites floods it) and push the labelled panic button (fear gas); (4) climb into the Exercise-Wheel Room and walk south five times to rotate the flood-hole to the top; (5) take the hundreds of quartz chips in the North Gadget Room -> dart chain reaction ('uranium/neutron'); (6) balance the three-disk block with the pebble on the middle disk, take the gold brick, and carry it north over the shaky South Branch pivot into the snake pit; (7) at the chasm, JUMP the bridge (the far rim is talc and you slide back); (8) fall in the glue pit, climb east and open the fur door so fur sticks to the glue (furry feet), cross the Glass Hall and take the silver necklace off the grounded iron shelf (static zap); (9) in the West Alcove turn the counterbalance crank down then up, giving the 'Exterminate' robot a free ride down to your level. After the 9th death the DM concedes ('Here is that #%$# key; take the coffin and get out!') and leaves the ornate iron key stuck to the Round Room ceiling. Take the key, go to the Great Door (n,e,e), unlock and open it with the key, go e into the Tomb and s into the Crypt, then push the solid-gold coffin (too heavy to carry) back along the only up route: north to the Tomb, west x3 to the Landing, then south into the Round Room. The moment the coffin enters the Round Room the obelisk lectures you to death with geometry ('...I love geometry... --end of session--') -- a deliberate parody of Infidel's downer ending, and the game's single terminal. Jericho 3.3.1 reports done=True victory=True at score 90/90 (max). Deterministic across two fresh replays (seed 1). Total inputs 99 (23 prelude + 76 commands); final input 'push coffin south'. Genuine authored WIN (WSL Jericho 3.3.1, FrotzEnv seed 10; byte-reproducible across fresh runs). Terminal banner "*** You have completed the first wave ***", score 19700 in 36 turns, reached exactly on the last input with no trailing command. Static proof that this IS the final win, not a checkpoint: the whole story file contains only three writers of the Inform deadflag (global G14) -- txd 10bc2 and 10bec store #01 (the two deaths: invaders reach your craft; an antimatter pod hits an undodged craft) and txd 10c33 stores #03. The custom DeathMessage routine 10b34 maps deadflag 3 to string S135 "You have completed the first wave"; deadflag #02 ("You have won") is never stored anywhere, so S135 is the only victory the game can print, and the closing S160 "SETI Command ... Waves of them, sir. No end in sight" coda is the author's sequel-hook joke, not a second playable wave (single room Cockpit, obj 25; no stage/wave counter is ever reset). Mechanics decoded from the per-turn daemon 10b64: the invaders sway between 1..G89(=6) and advance a row on each bounce, so row G8B hits G8C(=6)+1 on move 37 and kills you -- move 36 is the hard deadline and 35 gameplay commands is the longest possible game. FIRE sets G8E=random(2) flight turns and zeroes the missile offset G8F; LEFT/RIGHT shift G8F, the saucer offset G95 and the dodge counter G91 together, so a saucer hit needs G95==G8F at impact (i.e. fire while the saucer is "Directly ahead"), each hit scores 5000 and the third fires the endgame; a non-aligned impact kills an invader with p=0.5 for 100*row. A hostile launches with p=0.7 whenever none is in flight (G90) and kills you unless G91 != 0 when it lands, so every launch must be answered with a LEFT/RIGHT. 19700 = 3*5000 saucer + 13 invaders is the PROVEN maximum score for any winning line under this seed: a native re-implementation of the daemon plus the Frotz LCG (A = A*0x15A4E35 + 1; value = ((A>>16)&0x7fff) % n + 1, validated transition-by-transition against Jericho) was searched exhaustively with an admissible branch-and-bound bound (at most one missile impact per turn), and the frontier emptied with 19700 as the optimum. The last 3 commands are blank keypresses that flush the endgame's three @read_char pauses (txd 10c24/10c2a/10c30) which page the epilogue and print the banner. Jericho does not bind this game (victory()==False, get_max_score()==0, moves/score telemetry disabled), so the corpus audit uses a narrow guard requiring the custom banner, its score line, and the endgame prompt; deadflag G14==3 in RAM (0x08be) independently confirms the win.

Genuine authored WIN: the 56th and final input 'enter gazebo' prints the end-of-game banner '...you spend the rest of the night in literary ecstasy. *** You have won *** Would you like to RESTART, RESTORE a saved game or QUIT?'. Story defines no scoring (max_score 0). Jericho telemetry does NOT flag this win -- get_max_score()=0, victory()=False, done=False, game_over()=False -- so completion is established from the authored '*** You have won ***' banner, not Jericho flags (the game ends via a custom endgame routine + read_char menu). No RNG/clock dependence was observed (the moon/scenery are static); the full transcript is byte-identical across fresh-interpreter replays with and without a pinned seed (transcript SHA256 7d2ce0d9284d175c0a102f67db25fca8d63f0448f56fe3701e2ab10e7cff06e7 over 56 commands), so seed is left null. Story SHA256 dd77729c5096efff9b7dac4c6be9d46cb04e7193f4dac6f3d08724accc85d09f (moerike.z5, 71168 bytes). Theme: 1824 Tübingen; Eduard Mörike, a seminarist at the Tübinger Stift, must sneak out at night with room-mate Wilhelm Waiblinger to visit the mad poet Friedrich Hölderlin (who signs himself 'Scardanelli') in his tower on the Neckar, per a note found under the bed inviting them to Pressel's gazebo. Map: Dormitory-Hall-Gym-Shed upstairs (front-door street is blocked both ways by an impassable guard who confiscates carried items -- a dead end); the escape is out the dormitory window. Key puzzle chain: (1) The hall 'lamp' is a glass lantern whose candle is the ONLY portable light and is needed to see in the dark Shed; take the candle, light the Shed, and 'push trampoline east' to bring the trampoline (a pile of mattresses) from Shed into the Gym, then return the candle to the lantern so the Hall stays lit. (2) The Gym rope hangs from a ceiling bar too high to reach; stand ON the trampoline to reach the rope, climb up, and 'untie rope' -- you fall, but the trampoline (not the hard floor) breaks the fall, so you survive and keep the rope. (3) Back in the Dormitory, the rope tied to YOUR bed leaves the end 20 ft above the garden (fatal); the death hint 'tie the rope to something other than your bed' points to WILHELM's bed, which stands right next to the window, leaving only 8 ft (survivable). (4) Candle transport trick: you 'cannot climb a rope while holding a burning candle' (true for both the Gym rope and the window descent), and once out the candle cannot be relit ('nothing to light the candle with'); the solution is to THROW the burning candle out of the window first -- it lands in the garden still lit -- then climb down and pick it up, carrying a lit candle onward. (5) Board the wooden boat, take the pole and the tobacco; the Neckar current only allows travel downstream ('e'); punt east past the crooked tree to land at Scardanelli's tower. (6) Drop the pole, exit, enter the massive door; you must 'close massive door' before going up (the landlord shouts through the oak door), which makes the interior dark -- the carried lit candle lets you climb the spiral stair (otherwise 'afraid to climb stairs in the dark'). (7) Upstairs in the Study, Scardanelli is writing; 'show note to scardanelli' makes him say 'Let's go' and follow you. (8) Lead him down, out, and by boat downstream to the bridge (the land path tower->bridge is one-way and blocked in reverse), land at the Bottom of stairs, go up onto the Neckar bridge, north to Pressel's garden, and 'enter gazebo': with BOTH Scardanelli AND Wilhelm Waiblinger present the win fires. Arriving at the gazebo WITHOUT Scardanelli only yields Wilhelm's 'Pity you didn't bring Scardanelli with you' (not a win), so bringing Hölderlin is the authored best ending. The story's own 'walkthrough' verb only tells you to replay an external file 'moerike.lis' (not bundled), so this solution was derived entirely by direct play + static object-table analysis, no external walkthrough.

NINE POINTS (a demonstration/sample IF game by Robert Janelle and Brad O'Donnell). You explore your late great uncle's house hunting for his valuables; the lounge/trophy-room door has jammed shut. You start in the Hallway carrying a bottle of indigestion pills. Go N into Great Uncle's Bedroom (the door slams shut behind you -- you're now sealed in and 'sworn not to leave until you find some treasure'). It is dark: TAKE LANTERN (from the antique bed) and TURN ON LANTERN (+2). Reading the diary (found under the bed) reveals the uncle sealed his last treasure -- a bejewelled gold crown -- inside a secret room. To open the secret room: the bookcase sits on rails, but it's held in place; TAKE LOOSE BOOK (spine reads 'Murphy's Laws of Interactive Fiction') to leave a dark hole, then X POT (a ceramic pot; examining it reveals and gives you a rusty key, +1), then PUSH BOOKCASE to slide it aside, revealing a dark passage E to the Treasure Vault (+2). Go E, UNLOCK CHEST WITH KEY, OPEN CHEST, TAKE CROWN (+2). Return W to the bedroom; the south door is still jammed, so OPEN WINDOW (+1) and CLIMB THROUGH WINDOW down the fire escape. A twist ending fires (thugs mug you and swap the crown for a Minoan sceptre) but the game completes: '*** You have finished this sample game *** ... you scored 8 out of a possible 8, in 13 turns.' A full 8/8 completion. txd/infodump: objects include Treasure Vault[43] > treasure chest[44] > bejewelled gold crown[45]; rusty key hidden in the ceramic pot; bookcase[30] on rails[34].

Ninja's Fate by Hannes Schueller (Inform 7, 2010) -- an interactive tribute to Paul Allen Panks. Genuine authored terminal: the mission-success ending 4/6, 'Mission accomplished, but hearts broken', which the game's own shipped Hints menu defines as 'you have successfully retrieved the idol. Good work!' -- i.e. the best/winning route (the actual quest goal). Solved by normal play plus the shipped in-game Hints (the only allowed walkthrough source); no external walkthrough, no state mutation, no debug verbs. Route: the ninja retrieves the stolen village idol from a museum. Break the servants' side-door lock with the kunai (the gate is unbreakable, the roof trap-door needs the grappling hook), enter via the Storage Room to the Entrance Hall, go north to the 'Life & Works' hub, then north into the Ninja Room. There a dragon guards the idol inside a locked glass box while playing Spacewar on a PDP-1. Talk to the dragon and accept ('yes' = first game, a loss); 'play spacewar' twice more -- you improve each game and win the third, so the dragon honourably presses the escape key to unlock the box, then vanishes. Open the glass box, take the idol, and walk back out the way you came (s, s to the Entrance Hall, e, e toward the broken side door). On the threshold the semi-transparent ghost of Panks pleads 'Please don't leave!' -- answer 'yes' to keep faith with your village; step out to the Right wing, sw to the Front, then 's' down the southern escape route. The ghost whispers 'You make me sad...' and you carry the idol home; the elders are proud. The final gameplay command 's' prints '*** Mission accomplished, but hearts broken (ending 4/6) ***' then 'In that game you scored 501 out of a possible 1000, in 18 turns.' and the RESTART/RESTORE/QUIT/UNDO menu. IMPORTANT: this route deliberately avoids the west 'Westfront' wing, which is a procedurally-RANDOMISED maze (a parody of Panks' games) -- so the entire solution is deterministic (verified identical under seeds 1, 2, 999). Jericho reports the game as not fully supported and victory()=False, so classification rests on the banner + score line + end menu, not victory(). 20 commands, no prelude. No command follows the terminal 's'. PARSER GUARD NEEDED (documented, not applied per ownership rules): tools/replay_walkthrough.py should register a guarded WON rule, e.g. return 'won' when '*** mission accomplished, but hearts broken (ending 4/6) ***' in lower and 'you take the idol back to your shrine' in lower (guarded against false positives; the RESTART/RESTORE/QUIT/UNDO menu also follows). Until that is added the shared parser returns None for this custom banner.

Nostradamus's Onion Sandwich by David A. Cornelson (SpeedIF 4, 1999). You're atop the Eiffel Tower in 2042; Nostradamus wants an onion for his world-saving sandwich. Two hazards: (1) walking out to the Outer Rail can randomly throw you over ('your stomach churns up this morning's cheese sandwich' -> *** You have died ***); PUSH BUTTON first dispenses and drinks a glass of orange juice ('You feel much better as well'), which settles your stomach and removes that random death, making the rail traversal deterministic. (2) The onion has a smell timer that eventually blinds you and topples you over the rail, so reach Nostradamus in a few turns. SEARCH COUNTER yields the small onion (its only source). Cross the tower: EAST to Outer Rail (east), then NORTHWEST to OuterRail (west). Nostradamus sits on a cloud off to the west and is only brought into parser scope by LOOK WEST (which also shows him asking for an onion). Then GIVE ONION TO PROPHET (the parser noun 'nostramda'/'prophet' -> object 29; win routine R0291 fires on verb give/show of the onion, setting deadflag G14=2) -> 'You hand the onion to Nostradamus, he makes his sandwich, and the world is saved ...' *** You have won ***. Pinned to seed 12345 for reproducibility (the OJ removes the RNG death, but the seed is recorded per convention); Jericho does not bind this game, so the win is detected from the standard banner.

OnNoEf ('An Interactive lack of sense', 1999) -- an absurdist game where every action prints a Nostradamus quatrain. You start atop a nameless Paris tower (the Eiffel Tower); 'something is obviously very wrong'. Nostradamus sits in the Bathroom at the tower's base, with an onion. Solution: climb down the ladder (down), enter the bathroom (west), rouse Nostradamus (wake nostradamus) so the onion becomes available, take the onion, go back east and up to the Top of Tower, then step off in any compass direction (north) -- 'you leap off the tower'. Leaping while holding the onion (R0272 checks the onion is in object G12, the player) sets deadflag=2 and wins with the quatrain 'A scythe joined with a pond in Sagittarius...'; leaping without it just goes splat (death). '*** You have won ***', 7 commands, deterministic.

Order by John Evans (IFComp 2004). Deadflag win, no score. You are a summoned spirit with the power to CREATE objects out of magic. Escape the Bare Room (create key, unlock door). Defeat four elemental monsters, but the LAST one killed must die via a create-attack because that is what spawns the gerbil 'horde' -- so kill the AIR elemental first (roof steeple: create grappling hook, up, break windows with hammer, create duct tape, put duct tape on crystal) since its duct-tape kill does NOT spawn the horde. Then FIRE (Fields: create water), EARTH (Enclave Grounds: hit with hammer), and WATER LAST (North End: create ice) which spawns the horde at the Edge of the Grounds. Kill the horde with three DISTINCT attacks (it adapts: hammer, fire, acid). Then go to the White House, step to North End and back (n->laughter trigger, w) to summon Pire; wait for him to materialise (z z z) then CREATE EARTH -- an instant win that collapses the ground under his house (routine R at txd L0070: create earth/ground/land while Pire is in White House sets deadflag=3). The five-distinct-attacks brute force also works but the create-earth kill is a robust one-move finish. Seed-independent.

(2) Trap Maggie: fetch the green paperclip from the Toy Room (enter via Other Toy Room then down), drop it in the Main Hallway so its mirror the red key appears in the Other Main Hallway, unlock the red door, take the doll (Maggie's parallel) from the Other Front Desk and drop it in the Desolate Room. (3) Disable the lobby door alarm: carry the teddy bear (whose mirror is the monster/mine) into the Lobby and drop it. (4) Walk north to the Street. Scores 150/150 in 32 turns, rank 'You're free'.

Perilous Magic (A Really Short Interactive Comic Tragedy) by David Fillmore, 1999, Release 10 / Serial 990821 / Inform v6.21. Route/puzzle: the job is to triplicate the report in your cubicle, but you're out of paper, so you must cast the triplicate spell 'zemdor' on the report. (1) 'search junk' in Your Cubicle yields the old zimbor scroll (+1). (2) Go east x2 to Gunther's Cubicle and 'take new scroll' -- the zemdor 'turn original into triplicate' scroll. (3) The report cannot be carried ('you'll only lose it'), and the scroll must be brought home past Gunther. Trying to leave holding his scroll makes Gunther walk in and block you (location property 0x51 state machine, txd routine R0277). The key: 'give old scroll to gunther' -- the give handler (R0273) accepts any scroll-attr item, sets prop 0x51=3, sends the given item to his desk, and pushes YOU into the hallway (+1) while you KEEP the new zemdor scroll. (4) 'west' to Your Cubicle, then 'cast zemdor on report' consumes the scroll (+1) and triplicates the report -> victory (R0306: target report #1c -> STORE G14,#02, print S222). Jericho FrotzEnv.victory()/done stay False for this title (its custom end screen isn't auto-detected), so the win is evidenced by the deadflag=2 banner and 3/3 score, corroborated by disassembly. Deterministic: 2 fresh replays identical. story sha256 292b38a477a5b5ec3eef7ef356b0bba22a420b1a1f0a33c24d72b36a59d3367d; transcript sha256 17cc74a650f6307d114e2d6b015c5ccfdd13c0cb43e7469222fcf6a5248cbdd5. No RNG/clock dependence, so no seed pin needed.

Samhain by Eddie Mueller. ENDED, NOT WON -- this game is provably unwinnable and this route is recorded as a terminal ('died') result, not a victory. Proof: deadflag is global G13 (Z-machine variable 0x23, address 0x0fae; the library banner routine tests it for 1='You have died', 2='You have won', >2=custom), and the entire code region 0x309c-0xbe40 contains exactly three writes to it -- 0x0b675, 0x0b681, 0x0b693 -- all 'STORE G13,#01'. There is no 'deadflag = 2', no 'deadflag > 2', no '-> G13' result store, and no STOREW/STOREB with a constant base inside the globals table (0x0f88-0x1166). The status line's 'out of a possible 666' is a gag: the only score awards are the stock library +4/+5, both gated on the 'scored' attribute (#18), which NO object in the 80-object table carries, and Achieved() has zero call sites -- so score (G0d, 0x0fa2) is pinned at 0 in every reachable state. Route: ten WAITs let the scripted prologue run (a customer picks you up, the farmer's wife's misfired hex decapitates him, the head is sold off, and she grafts you onto the corpse); then E/N/E to the school, KICK DOOR (it is locked and OPEN DOOR fails), and in past the chemistry lab to the gym. All five cheerleader kills use plain ATTACK and are strictly ordered by the '[You hear X in the distance]' cues: shower room -> theatre -> cafeteria -> the dark hallway with the locker -> the gym. The fifth victim is Bjork, who carries the only three terminals in the game, all deadflag=1: KISS BJORK (used here), ATTACK BJORK and TASTE BJORK. KISS BJORK is the best of the three -- it is the only ending in which the protagonist completes the spree before the porn-flick's director calls the cops and he is executed ('Mmmmmm, pumpkin pie.'), and the game's own Footnote Fifty advertises it as a Special Edition Director's Cut ending while framing ATTACK as a mistake ('Idiot!'). Terminal banner: '*** You have died *** In that game you scored 0 out of a possible 666, in 34 turns.' seed=1 is required: Jericho's FrotzEnv.seed() does `seed = seed or bindings.get('seed', -1)`, so the previous checkpoint's falsy seed 0 collapsed to -1 (time-seeded) and did not replay byte-identically; the cosmetic '[PJ Harvey ...]' flavour daemon is the only RNG consumer, and the route reaches the same terminal under seeds 0, 1 and 42.

No title-screen keypress (prelude empty); the two trailing ' ' commands are literal SPACE keypresses draining the end-cutscene 'press SPACE to continue' pauses -- preserve them verbatim. STORY: penniless Rinaldo takes Lorenzo's wager to spend the night in dead Count Ruggino's 'haunted', plague-crossed house. WALKTHROUGH: 'search fountain' then 'take brass' (the R-engraved key -- it must be revealed before it is takeable) and 'unlock/open door'; open the plastic poniard's secret compartment ('twist handle' then 'pull handle') for Camilla's sleeping pill; upstairs in the Bedchamber, swap the scary art -- 'take portrait' (revealing a satanic mildew stain) then 'put abstract on hook' to hide it; fetch the travel pillow ('look under bed','open suitcase','take pillow','put pillow on bed','drop suitcase'); the desiccated corpse in the armchair must be carried out piece by crumbling piece to the balcony until the room is clear (it is 'sensed' even under the bed, so pieces cannot merely be hidden there); resolve the whole branching memory-of-Lorenzo tree with a chain of 'remember <topic>' until only the intrusive 'memory of a bottomless grave' remains; then the bedtime routine -- 'eat sausage' (snack), undress and drop every garment/held item (clothes hung on the wall-hook read as menacing silhouettes, so drop them on the floor), 'get on bed','read worm' (the lurid paperback makes you drowsy -- it only works in bed and must then be set on the armchair, never left in the bed), 'eat pill' to quiet the bottomless-grave dread, and 'sleep'. You dream the surreal six-rats nightmare, 'awaken at sunrise', walk 'e' onto the balcony where a 'plague angel' seems to infect you -- then the prank is revealed (the angel, the papier-mache corpse and the spiked pill were all a jape by Lorenzo, Camilla and Viviana); a month later the real Pestilence kills Lorenzo and Rinaldo drives west to Avignon with Camilla. GUARDS: 'twist handle'+'pull handle' opens the poniard; sleeping is gated on being undressed, empty-handed, fed, having read in bed, a de-scared room, a resolved mind (pill) and the pillow on the bed; the corpse puzzle is the seed-sensitive part.

Route: (1) intro on rails (wait x6, stand) until the Gloss ship auto-lands; (2) east to Airlock, 'close helmet' to survive vacuum, wait then east into the pitch-dark landing bay; (3) suit lamps are duds, so 'follow railing' -> 'feel box' -> 'push button' lights the Landing Platform [+10]; (4) east to West Lobby, up to Solar Furnace Control, 'push switch' (SHIELD RETRACT); the tower jams, 'x tower' brings the piece of twisted metal into scope, 'aim mirror array at twisted metal' melts it [+5], then 'aim mirror array at tower' restores power and lights the station [+15 = 30]; (5) east, push the call button, board the monorail, drive east across the habitation cylinder to East Lobby, out, north into the surface elevator, 'push down button' -> scripted crash tears the spacesuit; 'take off spacesuit', west onto the city surface; (6) LOST IN STAR CITY voice maze: trudge (west x8, north x8) until the trudgery table empties and the voice becomes present, 'listen' twice, then home in south to the voice building at Avenue of Kuznetsov/Boulevard B; enter building, up x3 to floor 4, 'open 406', wait for the film to finish, 'take reel' [+50 = 80] (the treasure); (7) leaving the building starts re-entry; follow the smoke pillar (west x3, north x4) to the crash site at Avenue of Zaitsev/Boulevard B, 'climb track', up; the tunnel airlock bursts (wait), 'let go of railing' -> flung to Platform 6; 'open hatch', 'enter hatch' into the M-48 glider; (8) 'sit in seat', 'fasten belt', 'close hatch', wait until the moorings tear and flight begins, 'press red button' (JET IGNITION) to escape into open sky [score 100]; Star City explodes and the blast deep-stalls the glider (pitch -43, spd 89). FLIGHT SIM: recover by pushing the stick forward until pitch hits 89 and control returns; pull the stick back to exit the dive (airspeed caps ~800); level the wings (roll 0) and hold nose-up to bleed airspeed under 150; after 3 level+slow turns the game auto-descends to ~870 ft at ~109 kn; then push forward to a shallow nose-down (pitch +7) for a fast constant-speed descent and pull back once near 60 ft to flare to pitch <= 0. The M-48 lands safely on the Kazakh steppe (roll 0, speed < 150, pitch in [-25,0]); 'unfasten belt', 'stand', 'open hatch', 'out' steps onto the steppe holding the film reel -> *** You have won *** (100/100). Standard Inform 7 victory (deadflag=2). Fully deterministic under seed 1; verified via Jericho 3.3.1 batch replay with continuation draining.

Sunburn (Caelyn Sandel, 2015) is a short 'social justice horror' one-act. You are Laura, a trans woman and vampire, drugged and imprisoned by Paul (a man she rejected) in a corner office whose great windows will incinerate her at sunrise, with a fire crystal blocking the only exit; Paul has promised to return, sweep up her dust and sell it. Jericho reports max_score=0 and victory()=False because the authored ending prints a '*** ... ***' banner and drops to the RESTART/RESTORE/QUIT prompt rather than setting the Z-machine victory flag, but the game's own scoring caps at 5 and this route reaches the maximum, best whole-game ending. Route: TAKE PLAYER (Paul's recorded taunt/confession; +1, the point most solvers miss because the desk is otherwise bare). EXAMINE WINDOW then EXAMINE SILL reveals a silver key; TAKE SILVER KEY (+1) and UNLOCK DRAWER WITH KEY / OPEN DRAWER yields a can of pressurized, explosive spray laminate that only bonds to 'plastic leaf'. TAKE the can and the John-Doe business card (plastic leaf), SPRAY CARD to stiffen it, then OPEN DOOR WITH CARD jimmies the plasteel latch (+1). Go SOUTH into the hallway; a fire crystal wreathed in flame blocks the south (outer) door. THROW CAN AT FIRE CRYSTAL rolls the pressurized can under the crystal; retreat WEST into the tiny closet and CLOSE CLOSET DOOR, then WAIT — the can detonates and destroys the fire crystal (+1). Hidden, Paul bursts through the outer door (move 18) and paces into the office (move 20); WAIT three total, OPEN CLOSET DOOR, go EAST (empty hallway) then NORTH into the office where Paul whirls with a wooden-bolt crossbow and hesitates for exactly one turn. BITE PAUL: Laura feeds just enough to regain her strength, spares his life, and hauls him off to the police ('You like justice so much... Let''s go have a chat with the cops.'). Terminal banner: '*** You finished your dinner date ***', 'In that game you scored 5 out of a possible 5, in 22 turns.' Timing is exact: with TAKE PLAYER consuming an early turn, Paul settles in the office only from move 20, so precisely three WAITs in the closed closet are required before emerging or he intercepts and shoots you ('*** You were murdered by an entitled misogynist ***'); one or two waits, or skipping the closet, is fatal. Fully deterministic, no RNG (seed=0 is nominal). Rejected outcomes: escaping via the south door instead (4/5, 'You escaped being murdered', leaves without proof), biting without first taking the audio player (4/5), and every bad/death ending.

WHEEL by John Toomey (IF Art Gallery, 1999-2000, Release 3). NOT A WIN RECORD: this game has a PROVED structural no-win, so no victory is claimed. Proof (see manual_solve/sessions/wheel_r3/NOTES.md): deadflag is global 0x16 (identified from the Main epilogue at 0x6ee9/0x6ef4, where deadflag 1 prints You have died and 2 prints You have won); across the entire decoded code region 0x23fc-0xba72 there is not a single write to it (txd shows 20 reads and zero stores; an independent raw byte scan for store/inc/dec/inc_chk/dec_chk on variable 0x26 finds none; every constant-base storew/storeb targets 0x0950 or higher, i.e. above the globals table which ends at 0x0950). Score is global 0x10 and can only change through the stock Achieved hooks at 0x70fb and 0x97d4, both gated on attribute 18 (scored), which neither object 24 (the gallery) nor object 25 (the wheel) carries -- so the score is frozen at 0 out of 0. DeathMessage (0xac40) and Amusing (0xac50) are empty rfalse stubs, so there is no custom terminal either; the only quit opcode is stock QuitSub. Confirmed empirically with RAM instrumentation (FrotzEnv.get_state()[0] is the 4540-byte dynamic-memory image, so globals are readable at 0x0770+2n): deadflag and score stayed 0 across 3070 single-step probes covering every dictionary word by ten noun phrasings, 40 random walks of 80 steps, 400 consecutive spins, and this 37-command route. The whole game is one room, one wheel, and three content routines (0xa99c gallery before, 0xaa40 wheel description, 0xaa7c wheel before) plus four custom actions (spin, rotate, xyzzy, help); spinning just draws three random(50) values and prints The noun verb adverb. This command list is therefore the complete authored interaction -- playing the wheel out -- and fires every authored string S110-S128: the wheel description and generated sentence, all four spin verbs (spin/turn/push/pull), every custom refusal on the wheel and in the gallery, score/full, the xyzzy easter egg (it stores 51 into the wheel-state global g00, and because the description tests g00 > 50 the wheel then reads The voice speaks hollowly until respun), and finally HELP, the author afterword that the game banner itself designates as the terminus (When you feel you have played the wheel out, try HELP). The list stops on HELP so the final observation is the afterword; it leaves a static press-SPACE read_char prompt which the shared harness auto-drains. seed=1 is MANDATORY and replaces the previous seed 0: Jericho does seed = seed or bindings.get(seed, -1), so 0 is falsy and degrades to wall-clock, and since every spin consumes four random() draws the old seed-0 checkpoint replayed differently every time. Two fresh replays with seed 1 are byte-identical.

Spodgeville Murphy and The Jewelled Eye of Wossname (David Fillmore, 1999) — an Indiana-Jones parody. wump2ka = 'Wumpus 2000' (Muffy St. Bernard / Andrew Plotkin engine), a large survival cave crawl. Solved BY HAND (live Jericho 3.3.1 replay + save-state branching + txd/infodump disassembly), NOT from any walkthrough. Pinned to seed 400 because the endgame depends on the Z-machine RNG (object-'bag' float daemons, ooze poison, monster wandering, and combat are all random()-driven). prelude = the title dismissal ('no' to the intro question + 3 keypresses to clear the title screens). ROUTE: an objectbag daemon floats the spiked shoes to Room #41 and the gas mask to Room #72; camp/relight to take+wear both (they gate every steep climb and the #72 pocket). Detour back to start Room #7 for the Transmat Popper + food pellets + canteen. All toxic-ooze barrels self-hole on a global turn daemon; with the gas mask on, drink L1..L5 ooze (ginko bars + food sustain hunger, the master resource - hunger 0 = instant death) to raise max-HP to 500, then descend to the L4 Room #64 hub. Route #64->#97, wait 2 turns so the wandering guard (obj311) leaves, enter multi-section Room #90 peacefully, take the quantum spike (obj296, ~500 dmg/hit), one-shot the dormant guard 'Dana' (obj312), and eat gbar4 (obj207) for +hunger and +50 max-HP (->550). Kill Boga at #86 (drops the red key) and the Wumpus at #98 (lead key; entered with NO regen = the surviving RNG alignment, ~11 spike hits). At #57 'search river' reveals the hidden underwater Hurkle; kill it for the blue key. Return to #90 and operate the iron door: 'put <lead/red/blue> key in keyhole' x3, 'turn <lead/red/blue> key' x3 (the third turn slides the door bolt back), then 'open iron door' -> the Emergency-Exit utility-room close, 'You have survived, you have escaped', and the final score prompt ('In that game you scored a total of 1116 points in 285 turns.'). Jericho does not bind this title (UnsupportedGameWarning), so victory()/get_score()/game_over() stay False/0 EVEN at the win; the authoritative proof is the terminal utility-room / Emergency-Exit text plus the final score/restart prompt. Exact parity: 311 stored inputs = 4 prelude + 307 gameplay, with 3 explicit [ENTER] blanks, and the final gameplay input is 'open iron door'. ENDED (authored, non-victory terminal). WURM ('A blatant abuse of the Z-Machine' by C.V.F. Knight) is a real-time Nibbles/snake arcade game drawn with direct set_cursor/print_char screen writes; on start it warns 'Your interpreter is unable to display this game.' but still runs. Static analysis with txd -a shows there is NO win state: the main loop r0014 clears a board of digit 'food' tiles and, when a level is cleared, does 'inc g04' (label l0003) to build the next, harder level forever; the score globals are g5=score and g6=champ/best. The only authored terminal is routine r0005 label l0009, which prints 'Your best score was ' + g6 + '.  Pathetic.' and executes the `quit` opcode. That branch is reached by the 'N' key, which the shipped on-screen HUD documents as 'N=endlevel' (r0005 maps 'N'/ESC/0xbc to l0009) - a normal documented player control, not a debug/cheat input. Route: input 1 is an empty line (a keypress) that dismisses the '[press a key]' title and primes the play loop; input 2 'N' ends the game and prints the banner 'Your best score was 0.  Pathetic.' (the trailing '9' in Jericho's capture is a status-cell rendering artifact from set_cursor, not part of the banner). No RNG is consumed before the terminal, so the outcome is seed-independent (verified byte-identical under seeds 0/1/2/7); seed 0 is pinned by convention. Deterministic: two fresh replays produce the identical banner. Jericho reports victory()=False and max score 0, consistent with an arcade game that has an authored end screen but no victory deadflag. There is no reachable 'won' terminal in this game; this best-score quit screen is the genuine authored ending.

WON. CAMEL (Creative Computing; z-machine port by Adam Biltcliffe). Goal: cross 200 miles of the Gobi desert. Static analysis with txd -a maps the numeric-menu command globals: g2=miles, g0=thirst counter, g1=water/drinks, g5=camel fatigue, g6=pygmy grace counter. Win test is in main loop r0005: 'jg g2 #c7' (miles > 199) stores g7=2 and prints s009 = 'You win, a party is being given in your honour ....... / ....... the pygmies are planning to attend .......'. Death paths: fatigue g5>7 (r0019, camel collapses), thirst g0<0 (r0006), out of water (r0013). Full speed (cmd 3, r0015) advances 2*(rand(10)-1) miles but adds 3 fatigue; rest (cmd 4, r0016) zeroes fatigue; drink (cmd 1, r0013) refills thirst to 4 while water remains; oases (random event r0022) are the only water refill. Authored, deterministic route found by a survival policy (drink when thirst<=1, rest when fatigue>=6, else full speed) replayed live under a pinned RNG seed. First input 'n' declines the 'Would you like instructions?' prompt. The 32nd input '3' crosses 186->200+ miles and prints the win banner; the trailing 'Want a new camel and a new game?' menu is intentionally NOT answered. This build prints the custom win banner and loops to a new-game prompt rather than setting the Inform deadflag, so Jericho's victory() stays False even though the authored win terminal is reached; the win is evidenced by the banner text. Seed 23 is required: Jericho seeds the Z-machine RNG and this build is fully RNG-driven (Jericho's seed 0 is wall-clock/non-deterministic in this build, so a positive seed is pinned). Deterministic: two fresh replays at seed 23 both end on the identical win banner. Max score is 0 (game exposes no scoring object).

notes: ZOMBIES (Miniventure-style survival, Inform z3). Locked in the boss's office during a zombie outbreak; the win is to blow up the whole complex and escape. (1) Arm up: take bat, open desk -> 9mm pistol, search boss -> 9mm ammo, put ammo in pistol; the office door's lock is busted so 'shoot door' blows it open (a bat won't do it). (2) Warehouse N: take chainsaw (the ignition source later). (3) Kitchen: 'open name plate' (Mac hid it 'in plain sight') -> plain industrial key. (4) Shipping/Receiving: open the COMBUSTABLE crate (NOT with the bat -- that detonates it) -> small bag; 'open bag' = black powder (a makeshift fuse material). Also 'hit biohazard crate with bat' -> pig brains (zombie bait). (5) Unlock + enter the Janitor's Closet (Kitchen east) holding the explosives. Lay a continuous powder fuse trail with 'sprinkle powder' in EACH of the four 1f-flagged rooms along the escape path: Closet -> Kitchen -> Shipping -> Warehouse S (every room except Warehouse N / outside). (6) Warehouse S: the zombie (Tina) is 'focused' and deflects every bat blow, so 'drop brains' to distract her (she hunkers down to eat), then 'hit zombie with bat' for the one-shot beheading; 'search zombie' yields the outer door key; unlock + open the outer door. (7) Sprinkle the final powder in Warehouse S, then 'start chainsaw' -- its sparks light the far end of the fuse (lighting it inside the cramped closet, room 0x21, is instant death). (8) 'south' out the open outer door to The Great Outdoors: the fuse burns down, the complex erupts, you dive behind your Ford Escort and survive -> 'You have won'. Verified via txd: hit handler R0141 beheads only when the zombie's 'distracted' attr 1d is set; fuse routines R0160/R0161/R0162 require all four 1f-rooms sprinkled and that you light from outside room 0x21; R0163 spares you only in The Great Outdoors (0x33).
